label: Dataset ID
description: Dataset specification identifier
missing_rule: Always populated from the dataset specification
notes: System variable injected during harmonisation

label: Dataset name
description: Dataset specification name
missing_rule: Always populated from the dataset specification
notes: System variable injected during harmonisation

label: Participant ID
description: Study-specific participant identifier
notes: Numeric ids: sprintf("%.0f", id). Same id across a participant's waves; unique within dataset x wave x st_measure_id. Ids that restart per survey: build <year>_<id> in the tidier. Rows keyed by row position or a row counter: inferred; name the affected waves.

label: Wave
description: Study wave or collection occasion
missing_rule: Use NA (row unavailable) when the supplied data hold a single collection occasion, even if the study labels it a wave of a longer study
notes: Panels: the study's own wave label as the spec or data carries it (T1, sweep_3, Year 9, 2016). Repeated cross-sections: four-digit survey year; add a sample suffix only when one year fielded separate samples (2015_sample_1). A second report on the same occasion is a tagged measure (st_measure_id), not a wave.

label: Year data were collected
description: Calendar year in which the row's data were collected
missing_rule: Where a per-row date is missing, use the wave's modal fieldwork year; NA only when neither fieldwork documentation nor any publication of the data gives a year
notes: Per-row interview or visit year where released, from the component that asked the screen items (compatible). Otherwise the survey's own year label (compatible). A few missing per-row dates filled with the wave's modal fieldwork year leave the row compatible; give the count. A year assigned wholesale from wave labels or documentation is the modal fieldwork year, or the midpoint of a multi-year window (inferred); cite the fieldwork documentation. Fieldwork timing documented by the study's investigators counts even outside the supplied documents (e.g. a project description or funding report): each wave takes its documented year (inferred). Only where nothing documents when collection took place is the value the year of the earliest publication reporting the data, one constant for every row (inferred); cite that publication. Where a publication reporting the data documents an upper bound on when collection ended (e.g. a received or submission date) in a year before that constant, the constant takes the earliest such bound's year instead; cite the bound (DR-0005).

label: Trial arm
description: Trial arm the participant was allocated to, for datasets from controlled trials, randomised or not
missing_rule: Use NA if not applicable (i.e., not a controlled trial)
notes: Arm names from the trial's main outcome publication; Control for the control or usual-care arm. Arm given by a variable or by the provider's file or sheet split: compatible; decoded from undocumented codes (e.g. an id character): inferred. Arms assigned by the investigators rather than at random (whole classes, schools or practices allocated, or quasi-experimental sites in a trial that also randomised) are compatible; record the allocation design (individually randomised, cluster randomised or non-randomised) in notes and, where designs are mixed, which participants came from which. Not a trial: unavailable, note 'Not a randomised trial.' Covariate when pooling trial cohorts (DR-0001).

label: Survey weight
description: Main participant weight for the wave, as released by the study
missing_rule: Use NA if the study releases no weight or is not a survey sample
notes: Cross-sectional participant weight for the wave, not rescaled. Where only longitudinal weights exist, map one and say which. Replicate weights are not harmonised. Use the study's core release weight; a design weight fixed at sampling may be carried within participant to later waves (partial).

label: Survey stratum
description: Sampling stratum used for variance estimation
missing_rule: Use NA if not released or not a survey sample
notes: Values fixed at sampling are carried within participant to every wave, without a wave prefix, so a participant stays in one stratum. Repeated cross-sections prefix codes with the wave where the study reuses them across waves.

label: Survey cluster
description: Primary sampling unit (usually the school or area) used for variance estimation
missing_rule: Use NA if not released or not a survey sample
notes: School ids qualify when schools were the sampled units; partial where the design is not documented. Schools in a randomised trial are not survey clusters. Values fixed at sampling are carried within participant to every wave, without a wave prefix, so a participant stays in one cluster. Repeated cross-sections prefix codes with the wave where the study reuses them across waves.

label: Family ID
description: Identifier shared by participants from the same family or household (siblings, twins, children of one mother)
missing_rule: Use NA if the dataset never holds more than one participant per family or releases no family unit
notes: The study's own family unit as character (numeric ids: sprintf("%.0f", id)): a released family, household, questionnaire or mother id, or sibling-pair codes, the unit named in notes; children of one mother and siblings in one household both qualify. Twins and other multiple births share it; no row records twin status. Built in the tidier from a household roster or documented ids: compatible; inferred from matching household items: inferred. Every participant of a mapped dataset takes an id, children with no sibling in the sample included; constant within participant and unique within dataset only. Where siblings share one parent or household answer (one questionnaire covering two children), name the shared items in notes. NA where the dataset never holds more than one participant per family ('One participant per family.'). Not a sampling unit (see survey_cluster) and not a participant id.

label: Sample component
description: Separately recruited sample, cohort or sub-study within the dataset that the participant belongs to
missing_rule: Use NA if the dataset holds one sample
notes: The study's own label in English (e.g. 'national probability sample', 'cohort 2', 'boost sample'), constant within participant, each label described in notes (recruitment, years, instruments, selection). Use where one dataset id pools samples recruited separately: different studies, cohorts recruited in different years, a probability sample with a convenience or boost top-up, or groups recruited separately on different criteria (e.g. by weight status). Groups recruited together under one design from one sampling frame or screener (age or grade cohorts, age-specific interview files) are one sample. Label from a variable or file split, or built in the tidier from documented ids: compatible; decoded from undocumented codes: inferred. NA where the dataset holds one sample ('Single sample.'). Not a wave (successive years of a repeated cross-section are waves), stratum, cluster or trial arm. Records the component only: within-dataset standardisation and the dataset random effect are unchanged.

label: Parent or carer respondent
description: Which parent or carer answered the parent or carer questionnaire or interview on this row
missing_rule: NA on rows with no value from a parent or carer questionnaire or interview; Unknown when the row has such values but the respondent cannot be determined
notes: One value per row: the adult who answered the parent or carer questionnaire or interview on the occasion. Where different adults answered different parent components, the one who reported the child's screen time (st_responder 'Parent or carer'), else the main parent interview; name the others. Mother and Father: the mother or father figure as for maternal_education (biological, adoptive, step or foster; a parent's co-resident partner counts as a step-parent). Both parents: the source records a jointly completed questionnaire. Other carer: grandparent, other relative (an adult sibling included), guardian or non-relative carer; name the relationships in notes. A who-answered or relationship variable: compatible. An item recording only the respondent's sex: female = Mother, male = Father, proximate, item named; other or not stated = Unknown. A single informant fixed by protocol (e.g. mothers only): constant, inferred, from the design documentation. A dataset with no parent or carer questionnaire is unavailable ('Not collected.'); one that never records who answered takes Unknown on rows with parent- or carer-reported values, as the missing rule says. Where two parents each report on one occasion on the family parent-report rows (parenting, monitoring, parent-child relationship, family functioning and conflict), those rows take this parent's report and name the other as unused, never an average. Recorded per occasion, never carried (the informant can change between waves). st_responder keeps its single 'Parent or carer' level, and the maternal and paternal rows keep their own routing rules.

label: Age in years
description: Participant age at the observation in years
missing_rule: Use NA when age cannot be derived
notes: Decimal years at the observation. Dates, months / 12 or tenths: as is. Birth year and month with the interview month or a documented fieldwork midpoint: derive decimal age. Completed years: +0.5 (13 -> 13.5). Completed-year band a-b: (a + b + 1) / 2 (13-15 -> 14.5). Open band: inclusive bound + 0.5 (12 or younger -> 12.5; 18 or older -> 18.5). Survey year minus birth year: + (fieldwork midpoint as a fraction of the year - 0.5). No age item: centre of the sampled cohort's age at fieldwork, inferred. Keep values above max_value. Say in notes which kind the source is.

label: Sex
description: Participant sex or gender as recorded by the source
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Male and Female from a sex or gender item; name the item type and the reporter in notes. Other: any further gender option (non-binary, transgender, another way, self-described). Unknown: prefer not to say, a merged Other/prefer-not-to-say code, and codes no source document defines. A code merging Female with Other or unknown maps to Female (proximate; name the merge). Carry across waves by the carry-forward rule in the harmonisation guide.

label: Country
description: Participant's location at observation point
allowed_values: Albania|Algeria|Argentina|Armenia|Australia|Austria|Azerbaijan|Belarus|Belgium|Bosnia and Herzegovina|Brazil|Brunei Darussalam|Bulgaria|Cambodia|Canada|Chile|China|Colombia|Costa Rica|Croatia|Cyprus|Czech Republic|Denmark|Dominican Republic|Ecuador|El Salvador|England|Estonia|Faroe Islands|Finland|France|Georgia|Germany|Greece|Greenland|Guatemala|Hong Kong|Hungary|Iceland|India|Indonesia|Iraq|Ireland|Isle of Man|Israel|Italy|Jamaica|Japan|Jordan|Kazakhstan|Kenya|Kosovo|Kyrgyzstan|Latvia|Lebanon|Liechtenstein|Lithuania|Luxembourg|Macao|Macedonia|Malaysia|Malta|Mauritius|Mexico|Monaco|Mongolia|Montenegro|Morocco|Netherlands|New Zealand|Northern Ireland|Norway|Palestine|Panama|Paraguay|Peru|Philippines|Poland|Portugal|Qatar|Republic of Moldova|Romania|Russia|Rwanda|Saudi Arabia|Scotland|Serbia|Singapore|Slovakia|Slovenia|South Africa|South Korea|Spain|Sweden|Switzerland|Taiwan|Tajikistan|Thailand|Trinidad and Tobago|Tunisia|Turkey|Ukraine|United Arab Emirates|United Kingdom|Uruguay|USA|Uzbekistan|Vietnam|Wales|Zambia|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: UK: England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland wherever the data identify the nation; United Kingdom only where they do not. Sub-national samples and separately sampled territories map to their country, named in notes; Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan are values in their own right. No country variable: a constant for where data were collected, inferred, source in notes. Never emit a value missing from allowed_values; ask for it to be added.

label: Australian State
description: Australian state or territory where the participant was observed
missing_rule: Use NA if not applicable (i.e., not an Australian dataset) and Unknown if cannot be derived.
notes: Australian samples only; other datasets are unavailable ('Not an Australian dataset.'). Multi-country datasets: NA for non-Australian rows; Unknown for Australian rows whose state cannot be derived. Name the source (stratum, site, protocol) in notes. Sub-national regions outside Australia go to region, and Australian rows also fill region with their AU- code from the same source. Used to report state-relevant findings to NSW DoE.

label: Sub-national region
description: First-level sub-national region (state, province, territory or equivalent) where the participant lives, or the study's own grouping of such regions
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: The current ISO 3166-2 code of the first-level unit (US-CA, CA-ON, KR-11, DE-BY, ES-CT); a lower unit the code list names (e.g. a Spanish province) is aggregated to its first-level unit, compatible. UK rows take their nation (GB-ENG, GB-SCT, GB-WLS, GB-NIR), regions within a nation aggregated to it. Where the source gives only a grouping of first-level units (a US census region or division, regional blocks, a study's sampling regions), the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code and the grouping's English name ('US: South', 'JP: Kyushu'), the finest grouping released, proximate, grouping named in notes. School location stands in for residence (proximate), as for urbanicity. Places the code list does not name (towns, municipalities, schools) are never placed with outside data: Unknown. Every Australian row takes its AU- code (AU-NSW, AU-VIC, AU-QLD, AU-SA, AU-WA, AU-TAS, AU-NT, AU-ACT) from the source that fills state, which is kept beside it, and every UK row takes its nation's code, in wholly Australian and wholly UK datasets as in multi-country ones. Carried across gaps of 12 months or less (inclusive), otherwise Unknown (filled in the tidier). Region never fills urbanicity, ses_area or country.

label: Ethnicity
description: Participant ethnic or racial group, collapsed to the schema categories
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Map through the shared ethnicity lookup; resolve released 'other, specify' text through a dataset lookup. US: Hispanic origin first, then race alone; two or more races = Mixed; AI/AN and NHPI = Other. A Hispanic-origin item sets Hispanic only in US and Canadian samples; elsewhere use the race, colour or ethnic-group item. Parda, Coloured and mixed-parentage groups = Mixed. Groups with no schema category (Indigenous and Pacific peoples, Arab/Middle Eastern, Gypsy/Roma/Traveller) = Other (proximate). A parent's own ethnicity used for the child: proximate. No item: unavailable; birthplace, language (see home_language) or religion only: incompatible; never a constant from study context.

label: Participant indigenous status
description: Participant is Indigenous to the country of data collection, as reported by the participant or a parent
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Indigenous: the source's explicit Indigenous category (US American Indian/Alaska Native alone; Aboriginal/Torres Strait Islander; First Nations, Métis, Inuit; Māori; indígena). Groups Indigenous elsewhere (Pacific peoples in New Zealand) are Non-Indigenous. Non-Indigenous: any other answer to an item that offered an Indigenous option. Unknown: non-response, and sites whose item offered none. An item that forces multi-heritage respondents to one group outside Indigenous: partial. No Indigenous option in the study: unavailable.

label: Minority
description: Participant belongs to an ethnic minority group relative to the national majority of the country of data collection
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Non-minority: the national majority group (US non-Hispanic White; UK, Canada, Australia any White group; New Zealand European; China Han; elsewhere the numerical majority). All other groups, including Mixed and Hispanic, are Minority. Use the same item, free-text resolution and carry-forward as ethnicity. No ethnicity item: First- or Second-generation immigrant_background -> Minority, Native -> Non-minority (proximate); with parents' birthplaces only, both parents abroad (or one abroad and the other unknown) -> Minority, at least one born in the country -> Non-minority, otherwise Unknown (proximate); a direct item on membership of an ethnic or discriminated-against minority: proximate. No numerical majority (e.g. Brazil), religion only or language only (see home_language): incompatible; Unknown for such sites in multi-country data.

label: Immigrant background
description: Immigrant background of the participant, from the birthplace of the participant and their parents
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Native: at least one parent born in the country of data collection. Second-generation: participant born in the country, both parents abroad. First-generation: participant and both parents abroad. One parent's birthplace unknown: the other decides. Unknown: no parent's birthplace known, or no parent born in the country and the participant's birthplace unknown. Use the UK as a whole; Hong Kong and Macao in their own right. Parents are the mother and father figures the source records; partial when one is systematically unobserved (resident figures only, not interviewed, never asked). Incompatible: child birthplace, language (see home_language) or citizenship alone, or rows that can emit only Native and Unknown.

label: Born in country of data collection
description: Whether the participant was born in the country where the data were collected
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived
notes: From the participant's own birthplace; fill wherever it is recorded, including studies that also map immigrant_background. Use the UK as a whole (born elsewhere in the UK counts as Yes for a sample from one UK nation); Hong Kong and Macao in their own right. A constant Yes is allowed only where recruitment at birth in the country guarantees it (inferred). Carried within participant (carry-forward rule).

label: Language spoken at home
description: Whether the languages spoken in the participant's home are only the country language, the country language and another language, only another language, or another language with the country language not recorded
allowed_values: Country language only|Country language and another|Another language only|Another language, country language not recorded|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Country language: a language with official or national status across the whole country of data collection or across a whole first-level region (state, province, nation, autonomous community) as at data collection (e.g. English or French in Canada, Welsh in the UK, Catalan in Spain, Swedish in Finland); a language with official status only in some municipalities or an administrative area (e.g. Saami, Hungarian in Romania) is another language. Name the languages counted in notes; in multi-country data key them on country (inline map or dataset lookup). Country language only: no other language spoken at home. Country language and another: a country language and at least one other ('mainly English but also another', bilingual, 'equally'). Another language only: no country language. Another language, country language not recorded: the source records that another language is spoken but not whether a country language is too ('speaks a language other than English at home', 'not English only'). Items on the languages spoken in the home, by the household or by the participant at home, are compatible from any informant (record it). Proximate, item named: the main language spoken at home (country language = Country language only, which then includes bilingual homes whose main language is the country language; another = Another language, country language not recorded; 'equally' = Country language and another); the participant's own first or native language from any informant (coded as the main language); a responding parent's own home language; a count of languages spoken at home (one = Country language only, which then includes homes that speak only another language; two or more = Another language, country language not recorded); and a source coded against one country language that files another as 'other' (e.g. Welsh in a UK survey). Incompatible, item named: interview, survey or test language, a parent's first language, proficiency or fluency, languages the participant can speak, media language, language of schooling, and a parent's home language from a time before the child's household existed. Where items on one occasion differ, take the better-fitting item, then the screen-time respondent's report (st_responder), and name the others as unused. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule). Language items never fill ethnicity, minority or immigrant_background.

label: Area-level SES
description: Socioeconomic status for the area the participant lives
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Map a national area-deprivation or area-SES index of the residential small area (e.g. IMD, NZDep) on the index's national quintiles: the two least-deprived quintiles = High, the middle quintile = Medium, the two most-deprived = Low; a source already banded at these points maps directly. An officially designated neighbourhood type with a documented SES gradient may stand in (proximate; Medium not emitted). Settlement size, region (see region), urbanicity and school-level indicators do not map here. Record the index, its release and which end is most deprived.

label: Household-level SES
description: Socioeconomic status of the participant's household or family
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Low/Medium/High = 40/20/40 of the unweighted sample within wave (and within country or site where the measure is country- or site-specific); banded sources by ridit, fixed class schemes by their standard three-way collapse, subjective standing at the labelled anchors (household SES cuts in the harmonisation guide). Prefer, in order: composite SES index, equivalised income or income-to-needs, affluence/asset index, occupational class, subjective standing. Parental education alone, maternal employment (maternal_employment) and school-level indicators do not map here. Compatible: income, income-to-needs, affluence or composite measure with every level within 10 points of 40/20/40 in every wave; proximate otherwise.

label: Household SES Measure Name
description: Source measure used to derive ses_household
missing_rule: Name the measure on every row of a wave in which ses_household is derived, including rows where ses_household is Unknown; NA in waves where it is not derived
notes: Constant per dataset and wave, written '<type>: <measure>', type one of Income | Income-to-needs | Affluence/assets | Composite SES index | Occupational class | Subjective standing (e.g. 'Income: gross annual household income, 13 bands'). Status inferred. The cut rule goes in ses_household notes, not here.

label: Household registration status (hukou)
description: China-specific household registration category, which governs access to schooling and welfare independently of income or current residence
missing_rule: Use NA outside mainland China and wherever hukou was not asked (row unavailable), including China sites of multinational studies; use Unknown only when hukou was asked but the answer cannot be classified, including non-Chinese nationals
notes: Country-specific stratifier; NA for datasets outside mainland China. 'Residence' is the unified category created by the post-2014 hukou reform.

label: Mother's education level
description: Highest completed education of the child's mother
allowed_values: Secondary school or less|Post-secondary|Bachelor degree or higher|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Mother figure the source identifies (biological, adoptive, step or foster; resident only where the source restricts to residents); name the definition in notes. Secondary school or less = ISCED 0-3, including A-levels, upper-secondary vocational qualifications and apprenticeships. Post-secondary = ISCED 4-5 and tertiary study begun but not completed. Bachelor degree or higher = ISCED 6-8. A source band spanning two levels goes to the level holding most of its members (proximate). Don't know, not applicable, other or foreign qualifications and no-mother codes = Unknown. Map through the shared education lookup.

label: Father's education level
description: Highest completed education of the child's father
allowed_values: Secondary school or less|Post-secondary|Bachelor degree or higher|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Father figure the source identifies, defined as for maternal_education. Never substitute a non-parent carer; where the source does not say which carer is the father and one is inferred, proximate. Levels and rules as maternal_education.

label: Highest parental education level
description: Highest education level across the child's parents/carers
allowed_values: Secondary school or less|Post-secondary|Bachelor degree or higher|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Highest level across the parents or carers the source records, resident non-parent carers included. Use the study's own highest-parent variable when one exists. Otherwise take the maximum of the ordered source codes after dropping don't-know and not-applicable codes, so one known parent suffices. In waves where only one parent was asked about, emit Unknown. Levels and rules as maternal_education.

label: Mother's employment status
description: Whether the child's mother is in paid work at the occasion
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Mother figure as for maternal_education; name the definition. Employed: in paid work or self-employed, full- or part-time, including casual or marginal work, unpaid work in a family business and a job she is temporarily away from (leave, parental leave included, illness, holiday). Not employed: unemployed or looking for work, keeping house, studying, retired, unable to work, unpaid volunteering. Don't know, not stated and no-mother codes = Unknown. Reference period: now or the past week; a longer window ('employed in the past 6 months', 'employed 50 of the past 52 weeks') is proximate. A current-occupation item whose options include homemaker or not working maps those to Not employed and a named occupation to Employed ('other' = Unknown), proximate. The occupation of a current or most recent job, an occupational status index, and employment before or at the child's birth are incompatible, item named. Any informant (the mother, the other parent, the child); record it. A respondent parent of unrecorded sex or relationship used as the mother is proximate. The father's employment and the child's own work are incompatible. Status follows the categorical SES rule: compatible, or proximate for a stand-in source; never partial. Carried across gaps of 12 months or less (inclusive), otherwise Unknown, as household SES (filled in the tidier).

label: Mother's age
description: Age in years of the child's mother at the occasion
notes: Mother figure as for maternal_education; name the definition. Decimal years at the occasion by the age_years rules: completed years +0.5, a completed-year band a-b at (a + b + 1) / 2, an open band at its inclusive bound + 0.5, a birth year by survey year minus birth year adjusted by the fieldwork midpoint. Single completed years, survey-year differences and dates are compatible; multi-year bands and open bands holding more than about 5% of rows are partial. Her age at the child's birth (completed years +0.5) plus age_years is compatible, named. Any informant; record it. A responding parent whose relationship to the child is not recorded (sex only, or neither), used as the mother, is partial; rows whose respondent is recorded as male, a father or another carer are NA. The father's age is incompatible, item named. Values outside 12-70 are kept as entered and screened at analysis. Not carried: each wave takes the age at that occasion, derived from a birth year or an age at the child's birth where only one is asked; an age asked at one wave fills other waves as that age plus the change in age_years between the occasions, partial, the projection named.

label: Urbanicity
description: Urban, suburban or rural character of the participant's area of residence
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Map an official national urban/rural typology by its own levels, in order, keeping its own thresholds. Raw settlement-size bands: under 5,000 inhabitants = Rural, 5,000 to under 100,000 = Suburban, 100,000 or more = Urban; a band straddling a threshold goes where most of its population lies. Binary sources emit Urban and Rural only. School location or a sampling stratum may stand in for residence. A study-level constant (inferred) only when the design guarantees urban residence at the measured wave. Compatible only for a residential three-level typology; proximate otherwise.

label: Family structure
description: Family structure of the household the child lives in (main home where the child has more than one)
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Two biological/adoptive parents: both resident parental figures are biological or adoptive, even if a step-parent is also reported. Step family: two resident parental figures, at least one biological/adoptive and at least one step-parent or a parent's co-resident partner. Single parent: one resident parental figure, no co-resident partner. Other: no resident biological/adoptive parent (grandparent, foster or institutional care, step-parent only). Shared care: the main home; none identifiable = Unknown. Source cannot separate step-parents from parents: use the category its structure forces (never Unknown for one category only), name it, proximate.

label: Family: Number of siblings
description: Number of brothers and sisters the child has (full, half, step or adoptive, resident or not), not counting the child
missing_rule: Use NA if not available; an only child is 0
notes: All the child's siblings, resident or not. A count of the child's siblings is compatible; a count of the children in the family or of the mother's or responding parent's children, the child included, maps as the count minus one, compatible, inclusion named. An entered count is compatible, kept as entered with any top code named. Bands, including a response list with an open top level: closed bands at their midpoint, the open top band at its floor ('6 or more' = 6), partial; write the top band in notes. Counts of children or siblings living in the household (minus the child where included) and counts limited by age (e.g. household members under 12) are partial. A yes/no has-siblings item goes to fam_siblings_any, never here. Birth order and household size alone are incompatible, item named. Any informant; record it. Implausible entries are kept and screened at analysis. Carried across gaps of 12 months or less (inclusive), otherwise NA (filled in the tidier).

label: Family: Has siblings
description: Whether the child has any brothers or sisters (full, half, step or adoptive)
notes: TRUE if the child has at least one sibling, FALSE for an only child. A yes/no has-siblings item is compatible; a tick-box with no explicit 'no' (unticked = FALSE) and an item on siblings living with the child are partial. Where fam_siblings_n is mapped this row is unavailable ('Derive at analysis from fam_siblings_n.'), so only-child status pools across every holding; a yes/no item is then named unused in fam_siblings_n's notes. Any informant; record it. Carried across gaps of 12 months or less (inclusive), otherwise NA (filled in the tidier).

label: Family: Parental rules on screen time
description: Whether parents set rules limiting how much or when the child uses screens
notes: TRUE if any rule limits the amount or timing of screen use; content-only rules are FALSE here and go to fam_contentrules. Where asked per device, TRUE if any device has such a rule. Record the respondent and devices covered. A single item pooling content with amount or timing rules ('rules about what or how much TV') is partial here and on fam_contentrules. A parent's technical time limit (device or app settings, a time-limit service) is partial here and also fills fam_mediation_technical. Restrictive mediation scores (scales, released indices and graded items on limits, rules or permission) go to fam_mediation_restrict; a graded limit item (how often parents limit screen time) fills both rows.

label: Family: Parental rules on screen content
description: Whether parents set rules on what the child may watch, play or use on screens (which programmes, films, games, apps or websites, or age ratings)
notes: TRUE if any rule restricts the content of the child's screen use (which programmes, films, games, apps or sites, or age ratings), on any device, FALSE if none does; where asked per device or medium, TRUE if any has such a rule, FALSE if every answered one has none. Record the respondent and the media covered. Partial: an item on one medium only (which TV programmes, which games), a household item answered once for all the household's children, and an item pooling content with amount or timing rules ('rules about what or how much TV'), which is also partial on fam_screenrules. Where the child and a parent both report, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other as unused. Incompatible, item named: rules on amount or timing only (fam_screenrules), graded content-choice items such as how often parents restrict or who decides what the child watches (fam_mediation_restrict), filters and blocking software (fam_mediation_technical), and retrospective items.

label: Family: Screen device in bedroom
description: Whether a screen device (TV, computer, games console, tablet or phone) is kept in the child's bedroom
notes: TRUE if any covered device is in the bedroom. Record the devices the item covers; an item on one device only (e.g. a TV) is partial. A behaviour item that places a device in the bedroom (using it there, keeping it by the bed at night) is partial, TRUE for any use or occurrence.

label: Family: Age at first own mobile phone
description: Age in years at which the child first had a mobile phone (any mobile phone or smartphone) of their own
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered, and where the child has no phone yet; never 0 or the current age
notes: The child's age when they first had a mobile phone of their own (any mobile phone or smartphone); ownership itself is not this row (an item on whether the child has a phone is incompatible, item named). Compatible: the age at which the child got (bought or was given) a first own mobile phone, in completed years + 0.5 (as age_years), years + months / 12 or months / 12, or the acquisition month and year minus the birth month and year in decimal years. Partial: an item on smartphones only, the age the child was first allowed to use a phone, and the age at first use of a phone (not ownership). Where several qualify on one occasion, take a compatible item over a partial one (an any-phone item over a smartphone item) and name the others unused. An item pooling phones with tablets or other devices goes to fam_firstscreen_age, and this row is incompatible for it. NA where the child has no phone yet (a 'not yet' answer or a not-applicable code), never 0 or the current age; no 'not yet' flag is kept. Any informant; record it; where the child and a parent both report, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other unused. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule: observed values stay and other waves take the earliest observed value in wave order), except that a wave at which the child had no phone yet keeps NA: a 'not yet' answer at that wave, or a carried age above the child's age at that wave. Not a screen-time quantity: it fills no st_* row and does not keep a wave under the screen-wave rule.

label: Family: Age at first screen use
description: Age in years at which the child first used screen media on any device
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered, and where the child has not used screens yet; never 0 or the current age
notes: The child's age when they first used screen media on any device (TV, videos, computer, games, phone or tablet). Compatible: an item on first use of, or first exposure to, any screen, with ages converted as fam_firstphone_age (completed years + 0.5, months / 12). Partial: first use of one device or activity, or of some devices (e.g. computer, game console, smartphone or tablet, internet, video games), taking the earliest age across the devices or activities answered; and the child's age at the occasion (as age_years) minus a reported duration of use (years online, months of gaming / 12). Where an any-screen item is asked, it is used and device or activity items are named unused. Not first use, so incompatible here, item named: the age at a first own phone (fam_firstphone_age) and the age a child was first allowed to use a device. NA where the child has not used screens yet or reports a duration of 0 (a non-user), never 0 or the current age. Informant and carry rules as fam_firstphone_age: a wave at which the child had not yet used screens (a carried age above the child's age at that wave) keeps NA. Not a screen-time quantity: it fills no st_* row and does not keep a wave under the screen-wave rule.

label: Family: Frequency of co-viewing or co-use of screens
description: How often the child uses screens (watching, playing or other use) together with a parent or carer, or with a parent or carer present and supervising
notes: Screen use together with a parent or carer (watching, playing games, using a device or the internet together) or with a parent or carer present and supervising; any informant; record the respondent, the media asked and the recall; respondent and recall do not change the status. Verbal anchors, share-of-time anchors included, map by the wording of the Frequency-item rules ('most of the time' under 'all of the time' = Often); a source with fewer than five levels is proximate. Day counts without wording map by the day-share cuts of those rules (days per week / 7: 0 Never, up to 10% Rarely, up to 35% Sometimes, up to 70% Often, above 70% Always). Hours with a parent beside hours alone, asked over the same device scope, map by the share of screen time with a parent under the same cuts, partial; hours with a parent with no matching total are incompatible. Where asked per medium or device, take the most frequent level across them; an item on one medium only (TV co-viewing, co-playing video games) is partial. Where the child and a parent both report, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other as unused. Incompatible, item named: yes/no items, talking about content (fam_mediation_active), rules and limits (fam_screenrules, fam_mediation_restrict), monitoring that does not place the parent with the child (fam_mediation_monitor), screens used to calm, reward or feed the child, household TV-on time, and study indices.

label: Family: Restrictive parental mediation of screen use
description: Score on a measure of restrictive parental mediation of the child's screen use (rules or limits on how much, when or what the child may watch, play or use), where higher indicates more restriction
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and released study indices of restrictive parental mediation: rules or limits on how much, when or what the child may watch, play or use, checking ratings, reviews or suitability before allowing use, permission or supervision required before use, and rules a parent sets together with the child (e.g. the restrictive subscale of a parental mediation scale, a count of online activities restricted, a study's limits-on-media-time index), compatible; record the instrument, informant, media and scoring in fam_mediation_measure. A released index is used as released only where at least half its items were answered. Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded items of the type with no published scoring (complete-case), a single graded item (how often parents limit TV time, who decides what the child may watch), and a measure limited to some media (TV, video games or the internet only, or TV and games); where scored per medium, take the study's overall index, else the mean of the per-medium scores. Yes/no rule items count only within a published index; otherwise they stay on fam_screenrules or, for content rules, fam_contentrules. Any informant; where the child and a parent both report, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other as unused. Keyed higher = more restriction; reverse items worded the other way ('my child can use screens without any restriction'). Incompatible, item named: talking about or explaining media (fam_mediation_active), using screens together (fam_coview_freq), checking afterwards what the child did (fam_mediation_monitor), filters and technical controls (fam_mediation_technical), screens withdrawn as punishment or given as reward or comfort, a parent's own screen use or modelling, attitudes to whether rules are legitimate, the style of rule-setting without its extent, graded items asked only where a rule exists (how strictly it is enforced, who set it), retrospective items, and general parental monitoring or control scales not about media (fam_monitoring_parent, fam_monitoring_self). Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Active parental mediation of screen use
description: Score on a measure of active (instructive) parental mediation of the child's screen use (talking with the child about media content and use, explaining, evaluating or advising), where higher indicates more active mediation
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and released study indices of active (instructive) parental mediation: a parent talking with the child about what the child watches, plays or does online, explaining or evaluating content and characters, pointing out good or bad things, and advising on safe or appropriate use (e.g. the active or instructive subscale of a parental mediation scale, a count of active safety-mediation practices), compatible; record it in fam_mediation_measure. Partial: an index that pools talking items with co-use, content-choice or permission items, the mean of a study's own two or more graded items, a single graded item, and a measure limited to some media (TV, video games or the internet only, or TV and games). Discussion of media in the family that does not name a parent is partial. The released-index gate, per-medium, yes/no, informant and standardisation rules of fam_mediation_restrict apply; keyed higher = more active mediation. Incompatible, item named: rules, limits and permission (fam_mediation_restrict), using screens together without talk (fam_coview_freq), monitoring (fam_mediation_monitor), technical controls (fam_mediation_technical), encouraging the child to explore or learn online alone, helping the child find content on its own, and general parent-child communication or guidance scales not about media (parent-child communication scales go to fam_parentchild_rel_self or fam_parentchild_rel_parent as partial).

label: Family: Monitoring parental mediation of screen use
description: Score on a measure of monitoring parental mediation of the child's screen use (checking or keeping track of what the child watches, plays or does online, during or after use), where higher indicates more monitoring
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and released study indices of monitoring parental mediation: a parent keeping track of or knowing which programmes, films, games, apps or sites the child uses, and checking browsing history, messages, contacts or profiles during or after use (e.g. the monitoring subscale of a parental mediation scale, a count of monitoring practices), compatible; record it in fam_mediation_measure. Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded items of the type with no published scoring (complete-case), a single graded item (how often parents monitor the child's computer use), a household item answered once for all the household's children, and a measure limited to some media (TV, video games or the internet only). The released-index gate, per-medium, yes/no, informant and standardisation rules of fam_mediation_restrict apply; keyed higher = more monitoring. Incompatible, item named: rules, limits and permission, and checking ratings, reviews or suitability before allowing use (fam_mediation_restrict), talking about media (fam_mediation_active), using screens together or supervising while present (fam_coview_freq), filters, blocking, tracking and parental-control software (fam_mediation_technical), helping the child find content, and general parental monitoring or knowledge of the child's whereabouts, companions and activities not about media (fam_monitoring_parent, fam_monitoring_self).

label: Family: Technical parental mediation of screen use
description: Whether parents use technical tools to restrict or monitor the child's screen use (filtering or blocking software, channel or content locks, passwords, device or app parental controls, monitoring or tracking software)
notes: TRUE if a parent uses any technical control on a device the child uses (filtering or blocking software, channel, content or password locks, device, app or router parental controls, time-limit settings or services, monitoring or tracking software), FALSE if none is used; where asked per device, medium or tool, TRUE if any is used, FALSE if every answered one is not; a released count of technical practices is TRUE above 0. Record the respondent, devices and tools covered. Partial: an item on one medium or one tool only (internet blocking only, a TV channel lock only), a household item answered once for all the household's children, and an index that pools technical controls with enforcement or punishment items (TRUE where a technical item is endorsed, FALSE where every answered technical item is not). A released count that includes security software (anti-virus or anti-spam) is used through its technical items only, and the count and its security-software items are named as unused. A technical time limit also stays partial on fam_screenrules. Where the child and a parent both report, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other as unused. Incompatible, item named: rules and limits set without a tool (fam_screenrules, fam_mediation_restrict), checking afterwards without a tool (fam_mediation_monitor), security software alone (anti-virus, anti-spam), knowledge of, attitudes to or barriers to using controls, and screens or devices withdrawn as punishment.

label: Family: Parental mediation measure
description: Source measure, informant, media covered, item counts and item scoring behind fam_mediation_restrict, fam_mediation_active and fam_mediation_monitor
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any mediation score (fam_mediation_restrict, fam_mediation_active, fam_mediation_monitor) is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument> (<informant>; <media>); restrictive: <scale or items>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean|count>; active: ...; monitoring: ...', naming only the rows mapped and each instrument or informant where rows draw on different ones, then the reversed items, the missing-item rule, 'single item', 'household item' or 'study items, no published scoring' where they apply, and any change of items or format between waves; one value per wave where the items change. fam_mediation_technical, like fam_screenrules and fam_contentrules, is a TRUE/FALSE row that records its items in its own notes and is not described here. Status inferred; unavailable ('See fam_mediation_restrict.') only when all three score rows are unavailable or incompatible.

label: Family: Parent's own screen time
description: Time the responding parent or carer spends using screens themselves, on any device and for any purpose, on an average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes the parent does not use screens
notes: The responding parent's or carer's own screen use, never the child's; record the respondent. Hours per average day under the screen-time band and Non-users rules: minutes / 60; bands at their midpoint, open top band at its floor (write it in notes); weekday and weekend items (5 x wd + 2 x we) / 7. One item on all screen use is compatible. Partial: an item limited to some devices or activities (internet only, TV only), an item excluding work use, an item limited to use at home, a weekday-only or weekend-only item, and the sum of separately asked device or activity items, which can count concurrent use twice (write 'Sum of A, B' in notes). Where items cover both parents, take the respondent's own. Time spent with the child on screens goes to fam_coview_freq. Frequency-only, ownership and problematic-use items are incompatible, item named. Values above 24 kept.

label: Family: Parenting stress
description: Total score on the study's parenting-stress scale, where higher indicates more stress
notes: Generic row for parenting-stress scales (e.g. the Parenting Stress Index short form total or one of its subscales). Record the instrument and subscales in fam_parentstress_measure; standardise within dataset at analysis. A parent's own depression, anxiety or general distress scale is not a parenting-stress scale: it goes to fam_parent_dep, fam_parent_anx or fam_parent_distress and is incompatible here, named.

label: Family: Parenting stress measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind fam_parentstress
missing_rule: Should not be missing where fam_parentstress is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscales>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>'. Status inferred.

label: Family: Parent's own depressive symptoms
description: Score on a depressive-symptom scale the child's mother figure, or else the responding parent or primary caregiver, completed about themselves, where higher indicates more symptoms
notes: Generic row for a parent's own multi-item depressive-symptom scale (e.g. the CES-D or a published short form, the PHQ-9, PHQ-8 or PHQ-2, the EPDS, the DASS-21 Depression subscale), as the raw sum or mean the instrument defines, keyed so higher means more symptoms; short forms, item subsets and adapted forms are compatible when fam_parent_mh_measure describes them. A released score averaged or prorated over answered items is used only where at least half were answered. Parent rule: the mother figure's own score (as maternal_education: biological, adoptive, step or foster); where the source has none for the child, the responding parent's or primary caregiver's own score (compatible, since the row's description includes this fallback); another parent's score is named unused and never fills a missing mother's score. Name who answered in fam_parent_mh_measure, per wave where it changes. Only a scale completed at the occasion: one completed in pregnancy or at an earlier wave is incompatible on later waves, named; never carried across waves, and each wave's value stays with the parent who answered it. Where two depression scales were given on one occasion, keep the fuller published scale, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the other as unused. An instrument with published depression and anxiety subscales (e.g. DASS-21, PHQ-4, HADS) gives its depression subscale here and its anxiety subscale to fam_parent_anx; its total and other subscales (e.g. DASS-21 Stress) are named unused. Distress inventories (Kessler K6 or K10, GHQ-12, Malaise Inventory) go to fam_parent_distress and never here, as does a scale a study presents as depression but built from K6 or K10 items. Incompatible, item named: single items, a study's own items with no published scoring, cut-off flags, diagnosis, history, treatment and help-seeking items, and diagnostic-interview symptom counts or probabilities (e.g. CIDI-SF). Parenting-stress scales stay on fam_parentstress, and a parent's rating of the child goes to the child rows (e.g. mh_dep_parent), never here. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Family: Parent's own anxiety symptoms
description: Score on an anxiety-symptom scale the child's mother figure, or else the responding parent or primary caregiver, completed about themselves, where higher indicates more anxiety
notes: Generic row for a parent's own multi-item anxiety scale (e.g. the STAI state or trait form or its 6-item short form, the GAD-7 or GAD-2, the Beck Anxiety Inventory, the DASS-21 Anxiety subscale), as the raw sum or mean the instrument defines, keyed so higher means more anxiety; short forms, item subsets and adapted forms are compatible when fam_parent_mh_measure describes them. Parent rule, occasion rule, half-answered rule, two-scales rule and mixed-instrument rule as fam_parent_dep (e.g. the PHQ-4 gives its GAD-2 items here). Stress scales and subscales (e.g. DASS-21 Stress, the Perceived Stress Scale) are not anxiety scales and fill none of the parent rows; they are named unused. Distress inventories go to fam_parent_distress and never here. Incompatible, item named, as fam_parent_dep: single items, study items with no published scoring, cut-off flags, diagnosis and history items, and diagnostic-interview counts. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Family: Parent's own psychological distress
description: Score on a general psychological-distress inventory the child's mother figure, or else the responding parent or primary caregiver, completed about themselves (e.g. Kessler K6 or K10, GHQ-12), where higher indicates more distress
notes: Generic row for a parent's own non-specific distress inventory with its published scoring: the Kessler K6 (items 0-4, sum 0-24) or K10, the GHQ-12 (Likert 0-3, sum 0-36, where the items are released; otherwise as released, e.g. GHQ 0-0-1-1 scoring, 0-12) or the Malaise Inventory; record the scoring in fam_parent_mh_measure. Where the K6 was asked inside the K10, keep the K10 (the fuller scale) and name the K6 score unused. A scale a study presents as depression but built from K6 or K10 items goes here. Parent rule, occasion rule, half-answered rule and two-scales rule as fam_parent_dep. Depression-only and anxiety-only scales, and the subscales of instruments with published depression and anxiety subscales, go to fam_parent_dep and fam_parent_anx and never here; those instruments' totals, stress subscales and perceived-stress scales are named unused. Incompatible, item named: single items, a study's own items with no published scoring, cut-off or caseness flags and bands (e.g. a K6 serious-mental-illness flag), and diagnosis items. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Family: Parent mental-health measure
description: Source instrument, parent who answered, item counts and item scoring behind fam_parent_dep, fam_parent_anx and fam_parent_distress
missing_rule: Should not be missing where fam_parent_dep, fam_parent_anx or fam_parent_distress is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: One string per wave, one segment per mapped row: 'depression: <instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>, <parent>; anxiety: ...; distress: ...', naming only the rows mapped, as beh_atten_measure does. <parent> names who answered: the mother figure, or the responding parent or primary caregiver with the relationships where they vary between children. Then the reverse-scored items, the missing-item rule and any change of form or recall period from the published form. Status inferred; unavailable ('See fam_parent_dep.') only when all three score rows are unavailable or incompatible.

label: Family: Parental warmth - warmth or positive parenting scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of their own warmth, affection, responsiveness or positive parenting towards the child, where higher indicates more warmth
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of the parent's or carer's own warmth, affection, praise, responsiveness or positive parenting towards the child (e.g. Alabama Parenting Questionnaire positive parenting, Multidimensional Assessment of Parenting Scale positive parenting, Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire warmth and support, Parent Behavior Checklist nurturing, a study's released warmth scale), compatible, in any form or item subset; record the instrument, informant and scoring in fam_parenting_measure. Partial: an authoritative-style score that adds reasoning or autonomy-granting items (Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire authoritative), and the mean of a study's own two or more graded warmth items with no published scoring (complete-case). A released score is used as released only where at least half its items were answered. Keyed higher = more warmth; reverse items worded the other way. Incompatible, item named: single items, yes/no or two-point agree/disagree items, bipolar style scores (e.g. authoritative minus authoritarian and permissive), the child's report of parenting (perceived parental warmth goes to fam_parentchild_rel_self as partial), observer ratings, parent-child closeness scales (fam_parentchild_rel_parent), psychological-control and autonomy-granting scales on their own (no row holds them), and media-specific parenting (fam_mediation_restrict, fam_mediation_active, fam_mediation_monitor). Where two parents each report on one occasion, take the parent recorded in parent_respondent (the screen-time reporter, else the main parent interview) and name the other as unused; never average them. Where two scales qualify on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with more non-missing values, and name the other as unused. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Harsh parenting - harsh, hostile or punitive discipline scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of their own harsh, hostile, coercive or physical discipline of the child, where higher indicates harsher parenting
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of the parent's or carer's own harsh, hostile, coercive or corporal discipline (e.g. Alabama Parenting Questionnaire corporal punishment, Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire authoritarian, the Parent-Child Conflict Tactics Scale psychological or physical aggression scales, a study's released harsh-discipline scale), compatible; record it in fam_parenting_measure. Partial: a study's released severity index built from discipline-strategy items, and the mean of a study's own two or more graded harsh-discipline items with no published scoring (complete-case). The released-score gate, two-parent and two-scale rules of fam_parenting_warmth_parent apply. Keyed higher = harsher. Incompatible, item named: single items (a single spanking or hitting item goes to fam_physpunish), hypothetical-response checklists ('what would you do if ...'), non-physical discipline scales (time-out, removing privileges, ignoring), inconsistent or lax discipline (fam_parenting_inconsistent_parent), psychological-control scales (e.g. guilt induction or love withdrawal; no row holds them), the child's report of parenting or maltreatment, and observer ratings. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Inconsistent discipline - inconsistent or lax discipline scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of their own inconsistent, lax or permissive discipline (not following through, giving in, letting rules lapse), where higher indicates more inconsistency
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of the parent's or carer's own inconsistent, lax or permissive discipline (e.g. Alabama Parenting Questionnaire inconsistent discipline, Multidimensional Assessment of Parenting Scale lax control), compatible; record it in fam_parenting_measure. Partial: an indulgence-type permissive scale (Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire permissive), and the mean of a study's own two or more graded items of the type with no published scoring (complete-case). The released-score gate, two-parent and two-scale rules of fam_parenting_warmth_parent apply. Keyed higher = more inconsistency; reverse a scale keyed to consistency. Incompatible, item named: single items, poor monitoring or supervision scales (fam_monitoring_parent), harsh-discipline scales (fam_parenting_harsh_parent) and the child's report of parenting. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Parental monitoring - parental knowledge or monitoring scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of how much they know about, or keep track of, where the child is, who the child is with and what the child does, where higher indicates more monitoring
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of general parental knowledge, monitoring or supervision, not about media, in the parent's or carer's own report (e.g. Alabama Parenting Questionnaire poor monitoring/supervision, reversed; a parent form of the Stattin and Kerr parental knowledge items; a study's released monitoring scale), compatible; record it in fam_parenting_measure. Partial: scales that add child disclosure, parental solicitation or general rule items, behavioural-control or rule-enforcement subscales that share items with a monitoring subscale, and the mean of a study's own two or more graded or true/false items with no published scoring (complete-case). The released-score gate, two-parent and two-scale rules of fam_parenting_warmth_parent apply. Keyed higher = more monitoring; reverse poor-monitoring scales. Incompatible, item named: single items, monitoring of the child's screen, media, online or device use (fam_mediation_monitor; filtering or tracking software goes to fam_mediation_technical), rules on bedtime or homework alone, who looks after the child, and the child's report (fam_monitoring_self). Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Parental monitoring - parental knowledge or monitoring scale (self-report)
description: Score on the child's report of how much their parents know about, or keep track of, where they are, who they are with and what they do, where higher indicates more monitoring
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of general parental knowledge, monitoring or supervision, not about media, as the child reports it (e.g. the Stattin and Kerr parental knowledge items, a study's released monitoring scale), compatible; record it in fam_parenting_measure. Partial: scales that add child disclosure, parental solicitation or general rule items, behavioural-control or rule-enforcement subscales that share items with a monitoring subscale, and the mean of a study's own two or more graded or true/false items with no published scoring (complete-case). A released score is used as released only where at least half its items were answered. Keyed higher = more monitoring; reverse poor-monitoring scales. Incompatible, item named: single items, monitoring of the child's screen, media, online or device use (fam_mediation_monitor), rules on bedtime or homework alone, who looks after the child, parents' knowledge of the child's feelings, and parent-reported scales (fam_monitoring_parent), which never pool here. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Parenting measure
description: Source instrument, informant, item counts and item scoring behind the general parenting and parental monitoring rows (fam_parenting_warmth_parent, fam_parenting_harsh_parent, fam_parenting_inconsistent_parent, fam_monitoring_parent and fam_monitoring_self)
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any of fam_parenting_warmth_parent, fam_parenting_harsh_parent, fam_parenting_inconsistent_parent, fam_monitoring_parent or fam_monitoring_self is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument> (<informant>); warmth: <scale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; harsh: ...; inconsistent: ...; monitoring (parent): ...; monitoring (self): ...', naming only the rows mapped and each instrument and informant where rows draw on different ones, then the reversed items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the missing-item rule, 'study items, no published scoring' where it applies, which parent reported where two could, and any change of items or format between waves; one value per wave where the instruments or items change. fam_physpunish records its item, informant and recall in its own notes and is not described here. Status inferred; unavailable ('See fam_parenting_warmth_parent.') only when every row it describes is unavailable or incompatible.

label: Family: Physical punishment of the child
description: Whether a parent or carer physically punished the child (spanked, slapped or hit) in the recall period
notes: Binary behaviour row for a parent's or carer's physical punishment of the child: TRUE for any spanking, slapping or hitting in a bounded recall period (e.g. past week, past month, past year), FALSE for none; a count of times spanked or hit is TRUE above 0, and a 'does not spank' code is FALSE. Partial: a typical-frequency item with no recall period ('how often do you spank your child when ...'), TRUE above never; a published corporal-punishment subscale, by the multi-item composite rule over its items, or TRUE above its minimum where only the score is released; and lifetime or 'ever spanked' items. Any informant, compatible; record it and the recall. Where the child and a parent both report, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other as unused. Incompatible, item named: hypothetical responses to misbehaviour ('what would you do if ...'), ages first or last spanked, threats, scolding and other non-physical discipline, and items on violence between adults or by adults outside the family. Never carried across waves.

label: Family: Parent-child relationship - relationship quality or attachment scale (self-report)
description: Score on the child's report of the quality of their relationship with their parents (closeness, trust, communication, feeling understood), where higher indicates a better relationship
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of the child's relationship with, or attachment to, their parents (closeness, trust, feeling understood, alienation reversed), e.g. Self-Description Questionnaire I parent relations, the Inventory of Parent and Peer Attachment parent scales or an adaptation, a closeness-to-parents scale, a study's released relationship scale, compatible; record it in fam_parentchild_measure. Where mother and father are rated separately, use the mean of the answered parents' scores, named in fam_parentchild_measure. Partial: parent-adolescent communication scales, scales of perceived parental warmth or of warmth and hostility (hostility reversed), and the mean of a study's own two or more graded relationship items with no published scoring (complete-case). A released score is used as released only where at least half its items were answered. Keyed higher = better relationship; reverse alienation, hostility and conflict items inside a relationship scale, but a parent-child conflict scale is never reversed onto this row. Incompatible, item named: single items (one closeness item per parent stays a single item, even averaged over parents), satisfaction with family or with the relationship with parents (wb_domainsat_family_self), perceived support (wb_socsupport_family_self), family-climate scales (fam_functioning_self, fam_conflict_self), parental monitoring or knowledge scales (fam_monitoring_self) and parent-reported scales (fam_parentchild_rel_parent), which never pool here. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Parent-child relationship - closeness scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of the closeness and warmth of their relationship with the child, where higher indicates a closer relationship
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of the parent's or carer's report of closeness in their relationship with the child (e.g. Child-Parent Relationship Scale closeness, any form, released or scored from its items by the published key), compatible; record it in fam_parentchild_measure. Partial: parent-reported parent-child communication scales, and the mean of a study's own two or more graded closeness items with no published scoring (complete-case). A released score is used as released only where at least half its items were answered. Keyed higher = closer; reverse items worded the other way. Parent-child conflict scales go to fam_parentchild_conflict_parent and are never reversed onto this row; a study with both fills both. Incompatible, item named: single items, the parent's own warmth or positive parenting (fam_parenting_warmth_parent), family-wide functioning (fam_functioning_parent), parenting stress (fam_parentstress) and the child's report (fam_parentchild_rel_self). Where two parents each report on one occasion, take the parent recorded in parent_respondent (the screen-time reporter, else the main parent interview) and name the other as unused; never average them. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Parent-child relationship - conflict scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of conflict in their relationship with the child, where higher indicates more conflict
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of the parent's or carer's report of conflict in their relationship with the child (e.g. Child-Parent Relationship Scale conflict, any form, released or scored from its items by the published key), compatible; record it in fam_parentchild_measure. Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded parent-child conflict items with no published scoring (complete-case). The released-score gate and two-parent rule of fam_parentchild_rel_parent apply. Keyed higher = more conflict; never reversed onto fam_parentchild_rel_parent. Incompatible, item named: single items, child behaviour-problem scales (oppositional, conduct and other problem scales keep their own rows), family-wide conflict (fam_conflict_parent), harsh-discipline scales (fam_parenting_harsh_parent), parenting stress (fam_parentstress) and the child's report. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Parent-child relationship measure
description: Source instrument, informant, parents rated, item counts and item scoring behind the parent-child relationship rows (fam_parentchild_rel_self, fam_parentchild_rel_parent and fam_parentchild_conflict_parent)
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any of fam_parentchild_rel_self, fam_parentchild_rel_parent or fam_parentchild_conflict_parent is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: 'relationship (self): <instrument> (<parents rated>), <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; closeness (parent): <instrument> (<informant>), ...; conflict (parent): ...', naming only the rows mapped, then the reversed items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the missing-item rule, the averaging over mother and father where the child rated both, which parent reported where two could, 'study items, no published scoring' where it applies, and any change of items or format between waves; one value per wave where the instruments or items change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See fam_parentchild_rel_self.') only when every row it describes is unavailable or incompatible.

label: Family: Family functioning - family functioning or cohesion scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of the family's general functioning or cohesion (getting along, expressing feelings, closeness, solving problems together), where higher indicates healthier functioning
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of general family functioning, cohesion or family climate (e.g. McMaster Family Assessment Device general functioning, any length, reversed; FACES balanced cohesion; Family Environment Scale cohesion; Family APGAR; a study's released family-functioning scale), compatible; record it in fam_functioning_measure. Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded functioning items with no published scoring (complete-case). A released score is used as released only where at least half its items were answered. Keyed higher = healthier functioning; reverse scales scored higher = worse (e.g. the Family Assessment Device, 1 = healthiest). Family conflict scales go to fam_conflict_parent and are never reversed onto this row; a study with both fills both. Flexibility, adaptability, rigidity or chaos scales (e.g. FACES balanced flexibility) are named as unused. Incompatible, item named: single items, yes/no items, parenting scales (fam_parenting_warmth_parent and its siblings), parent-child relationship scales (fam_parentchild_rel_parent), couple-relationship scales, parenting stress (fam_parentstress), satisfaction or support ratings, and the child's report (fam_functioning_self). Where two parents each report on one occasion, take the parent recorded in parent_respondent (the screen-time reporter, else the main parent interview) and name the other as unused; never average them. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Family functioning - family functioning or cohesion scale (self-report)
description: Score on the child's report of the family's general functioning or cohesion (getting along, expressing feelings, closeness, solving problems together), where higher indicates healthier functioning
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of general family functioning, cohesion or family climate as the child reports it (e.g. Family APGAR, McMaster Family Assessment Device general functioning, any length, reversed; a family-environment or cohesion scale; a study's released family-climate scale), compatible; record it in fam_functioning_measure. Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded functioning items with no published scoring (complete-case). The released-score gate, keying and flexibility rules of fam_functioning_parent apply. Family conflict scales go to fam_conflict_self and are never reversed onto this row; a study with both fills both. Incompatible, item named: single items, yes/no items, perceived family support (wb_socsupport_family_self), single family-satisfaction items (wb_domainsat_family_self), parent-child relationship scales (fam_parentchild_rel_self), and parent-reported scales (fam_functioning_parent), which never pool here. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Family conflict - family conflict scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent's or carer's report of conflict among family members (fighting, arguing, criticising, hitting), where higher indicates more conflict
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of conflict among family members (e.g. Family Environment Scale conflict, any length; a study's released family-conflict scale), compatible; record it in fam_functioning_measure. Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded conflict items with no published scoring (complete-case), and a family-problems scale that mixes conflict with harsh-discipline or low-support items. The released-score gate and two-parent rule of fam_functioning_parent apply. Keyed higher = more conflict; never reversed onto fam_functioning_parent. Incompatible, item named: single items, yes/no items, conflict between the parents (couple-relationship scales), parent-child conflict (fam_parentchild_conflict_parent), harsh-discipline scales (fam_parenting_harsh_parent), violence by adults outside the family, and the child's report (fam_conflict_self). Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Family conflict - family conflict scale (self-report)
description: Score on the child's report of conflict among family members (fighting, arguing, criticising, hitting), where higher indicates more conflict
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales and subscales of conflict among family members as the child reports it (e.g. Family Environment Scale conflict, a study's released family-conflict scale), compatible; record it in fam_functioning_measure.
