Partial: the mean of a study's own two or more graded conflict items with no published scoring (complete-case), and a family-problems scale that mixes conflict with parents yelling or hitting or with reversed love or support items. The released-score gate of fam_functioning_parent applies. Keyed higher = more conflict; never reversed onto fam_functioning_self. Incompatible, item named: single items, yes/no items, conflict between the parents, parent-child conflict scales (no child-report row holds them, and they are never reversed onto fam_parentchild_rel_self), harsh-discipline scales on their own, violence by adults outside the family, the child's report of maltreatment, and parent-reported scales (fam_conflict_parent), which never pool here. Standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Family: Family functioning measure
description: Source instrument, informant, item counts and item scoring behind the family functioning and family conflict rows (fam_functioning_parent, fam_functioning_self, fam_conflict_parent and fam_conflict_self)
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any of fam_functioning_parent, fam_functioning_self, fam_conflict_parent or fam_conflict_self is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: 'functioning (parent): <instrument> (<informant>), <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; functioning (self): ...; conflict (parent): ...; conflict (self): ...', naming only the rows mapped, then the reversed items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the missing-item rule, 'study items, no published scoring' where it applies, which parent reported where two could, and any change of items or format between waves; one value per wave where the instruments or items change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See fam_functioning_parent.') only when every row it describes is unavailable or incompatible.

label: Family: Frequency of reading to the child
description: How often a parent or other family member reads books or stories to the child
allowed_values: Every day|Several times a week|Once or twice a week|Less than once a week
notes: Reading books or stories to the child, or looking at books together, by a parent, other family member or carer at home; record the respondent, ages and recall, which does not change the status. Day counts: 7 = Every day, 3-6 = Several times a week, 1-2 = Once or twice a week, none in the reference week = Less than once a week; counts of times read as days. Verbal scales map by wording; monthly, yearly, rarely, never and not at all = Less than once a week. A band crossing a level boundary (1-3 days, almost every day, 7 or more times) goes to the level holding most of it, proximate, as is a scale that cannot reach a level (name it); 'every day or almost every day' = Every day, proximate. Partial: the respondent's own reading only (where the same respondent also reports others' reading, take the more frequent), or reading pooled with storytelling or singing. Storytelling or singing alone, the child's own reading or book use (whatever the age), the child reading to others, library visits and retrospective items (age reading began) are incompatible. Minutes go to fam_readto_time.

label: Family: Time spent reading to the child
description: Time a parent or other family member spends reading books or stories to the child on an average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes the child was not read to
notes: Hours per average day under the screen-time band and Non-users rules: minutes / 60; bands at their midpoint, open top band at its floor (write it in notes); weekday and weekend items (5 x wd + 2 x we) / 7. Minutes per day or session of reading x days or sessions read to per week / 7 (day-of-use rule), partial; a day band takes its midpoint (3-6 days = 4.5), and a verbal frequency takes the days of its fam_readto_freq level (Every day 7, Several times a week 4.5, Once or twice a week 1.5); minutes with no frequency answer, or with a frequency below weekly, are NA (named in notes). 0 where a frequency or filter item says the child was not read to. Scope, respondent and pooling rules as fam_readto_freq (partial). Time pooling reading to the child with the child's own reading is incompatible. A frequency-only item leaves this row incompatible, item named.

label: Family: Number of children's books
description: Number of children's books the child has or that are in the home
missing_rule: Use NA if not available; 'no books' is 0
notes: Children's books the child has (including those shared with siblings) or children's books in the home; record the respondent and wording. An entered count is compatible, kept as entered with any top code named. Bands: none = 0, closed bands at their midpoint, open top band at its stated lower bound ('50 or more' = 50), partial; write the top band in notes. Top codes differ between studies; standardise within dataset at analysis. Total books in the home (adult books included), books read or borrowed, books in the bedroom and retrospective counts are incompatible, item named.

label: Family: Home environment - HOME Inventory total score
description: Total raw score on a form of the Home Observation for Measurement of the Environment (HOME) Inventory, where higher indicates a more stimulating and supportive home environment
notes: Named-instrument row for the Home Observation for Measurement of the Environment (HOME) Inventory: the released raw total of any published form (Infant-Toddler, Early Childhood, Middle Childhood, Early Adolescent, or a published short form such as the HOME-SF used in national surveys), observation and interview or interview only, compatible; record the form, age version, item count and administration in fam_home_measure. Partial: an adapted or translated form, and a total summed from a form's released subscales. A released standard score only where no raw score is released (partial); percentiles and risk bands never map. Incompatible, item named: a study's own home-environment checklist, unless its documentation shows it is a HOME form (then partial), and HOME items with no released total or subscale score. Full-form subscales (learning materials, language stimulation, responsivity, acceptance and the like) are used only through this total and are named as unused. HOME-derived single items with rows of their own (times read to, children's books) also map to those rows. The form changes with the child's age: standardise within dataset and form at analysis.

label: Family: Home environment - HOME short-form cognitive stimulation subscale
description: Raw score on the cognitive stimulation subscale of a HOME Inventory short form (learning materials, reading, outings and teaching items), where higher indicates more cognitive stimulation
notes: Named-instrument row: the released raw cognitive stimulation subscale score of a published HOME short form (e.g. the HOME-SF), compatible; an adapted or translated short form is partial; record the form and age version in fam_home_measure. A released standard score only where no raw score is released (partial); percentiles never map. Full-form subscales (learning materials, language, academic stimulation, variety) are used only through fam_home_total and are incompatible here, named. The items change with the child's age: standardise within dataset and form at analysis.

label: Family: Home environment - HOME short-form emotional support subscale
description: Raw score on the emotional support subscale of a HOME Inventory short form (parental responsivity, warmth, acceptance and lack of punishment), where higher indicates more emotional support
notes: Named-instrument row: the released raw emotional support subscale score of a published HOME short form (e.g. the HOME-SF), compatible; an adapted or translated short form is partial; record the form and age version in fam_home_measure. A released standard score only where no raw score is released (partial); percentiles never map. Full-form subscales (responsivity, acceptance, warmth, modelling) are used only through fam_home_total and are incompatible here, named. The items change with the child's age: standardise within dataset and form at analysis.

label: Family: HOME Inventory measure
description: HOME Inventory form, age version, administration, item counts and scoring behind fam_home_total, fam_home_cogstim and fam_home_emotsupport
missing_rule: Should not be missing where fam_home_total, fam_home_cogstim or fam_home_emotsupport is non-missing; NA in waves where no HOME form was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its form cannot be identified
notes: '<form> (<observation and interview|interview only>); total: <k> of <K> items, <item scoring>, sum (range <min>-<max>); cognitive stimulation: ...; emotional support: ...', naming only the rows mapped, then any adaptation or translation, the score form where a standard score is used, and the full-form subscales named as unused; where the form changes with the child's age, the forms and item counts by age group (as beh_parent_measure); one value per wave where the forms change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See fam_home_total.') only when all three HOME rows are unavailable or incompatible.

label: School grade or year level
description: School grade or year level at the observation
notes: The study's own year-level label, translated where needed but keeping system terms (Year 7, Klasse 5, 9th year ensino fundamental, 3ro ESO, Junior high 2); never renumber onto another system. One wording per school system across datasets (Korea: 'Middle School 1st Grade'). Grade fixed by sampling whole classes of one grade: emit it, compatible. Grade deduced from cohort progression or birth-date windows: inferred, and only where documentation names the grade. School-type or sampled age-group codes without a year level: incompatible (a secondary track or programme goes to school_track). For sample description only.

label: School sector (public or private)
description: Whether the school the participant attends is publicly or privately managed
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Public: managed by a government authority. Private: managed by a non-government body (independent, religious or parochial); government-dependent private schools, such as voucher or subsidised schools, are Private, proximate. Home-schooled or not enrolled: Unknown. School track or programme (academic, vocational, grammar) is not sector and goes to school_track. Never an SES indicator (see ses_household).

label: School track or programme
description: Track, stream or programme of secondary schooling the participant attends, ordered from most to least academically selective
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Academic: general, university-preparatory tracks (gymnasium, grammar school, ASO, a US academic or college-preparatory programme) and the highest lower-secondary stream. Intermediate: technical, arts or four-year vocational tracks leading to a university-entrance qualification, and middle lower-secondary streams (e.g. Realschule, a US general programme). Vocational: trade or three-year vocational tracks and the basic lower-secondary stream (e.g. BSO, Hauptschule). Not tracked: primary school, or a comprehensive school or system with no track at the participant's stage; a constant 'Not tracked' (inferred) only where the design places every participant at an untracked stage, source named. Map the study's levels in order and name the mapping; a system with more levels folds adjacent levels, proximate (gymnasium = Academic, Sek A = Intermediate, Sek B and C = Vocational; ASO = Academic, KSO and TSO = Intermediate, BSO = Vocational). Language-of-instruction tracks, specialist options not ordered by academic selectivity and special-needs programmes are incompatible, item named. Not yet at school, home-schooled, not enrolled or beyond secondary school: Unknown. Never an SES source (see ses_household) and never school_sector. Carried within participant while the participant stays at the same school stage (filled in the tidier), never across the move from lower to upper secondary.

label: Screen Time Measure ID
description: Identifies which screen-time measure a row carries when a dataset contributes more than one (for example a questionnaire and a time-use diary, or a parent and a child report). The rows derived from a datasets untagged variables.csv mapping are primary; rows produced by a measure tag in variables.csv carry that tag. participant_id + wave + st_measure_id identify a row.
missing_rule: Injected by the harmoniser, should never be missing
notes: System variable filled by the pipeline, not mapped in variables.csv. Filtering to st_measure_id == primary reproduces the one-row-per-participant-wave table.

label: Screen Time Measurement Type
description: Response format of the screen-time items on this row
notes: Continuous: open numeric time entry (hours or minutes), time-use diary or device log. Categorical: response bands, including bands the study or the mapping scores as hours. Where items of both formats feed a row, record the format behind its core st_ variables and name the other in notes. Vary by wave where the format changes.

label: Screen Time Measure Name
description: Instrument that supplied the screen-time items on this row
missing_rule: Should not be missing; use "Unknown" only when item provenance cannot be established
notes: One controlled label: the published name of a standalone instrument (e.g. "Questionnaire for Screen Time of Adolescents (QueST)"); "Time use diary" for diaries; "Custom" for items written for the study or its survey programme, including the study's own questionnaire; "Unknown" only when item provenance cannot be established. Never combined labels ("Unknown/custom") or "Custom: ..." variants. Item wording, codes and waves go in variables.csv notes. The method behind the st_violent_* rows goes in st_violent_measure, not here.

label: Screen Time Respondent
description: Who reported the screen-time values on this row
allowed_values: Self|Parent or carer|Teacher|Device or objective measure|Other|Unknown
missing_rule: NA on rows with no screen-time value; Unknown when the row has screen-time values but the respondent cannot be determined
notes: One responder per row: every st_ value on the row, and every filter question that sets one to zero, comes from that responder. Vary by wave or age where the respondent changes by design; with no who-answered variable, deduce it from which item series is answered and record the cut in notes. Primary rows carry the study's main series; a second responder on the same occasion is a tagged measure block (DR-0003). Never combine responders within a row or a variable.

label: Screen Time: Aggregated total on average weekday
description: Total time engaging in screen use on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_total; rules as st_total.

label: Screen Time: Aggregated total on average weekend day
description: Total time engaging in screen use on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_total; rules as st_total.

label: Screen Time: Aggregated total on average day
description: Total time engaging in screen use on a regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Not for the original IPD. Map one item on all screen use, or sum items the instrument defines as mutually exclusive parts of it (contexts such as location, learning vs leisure, alone vs co-use). Partial if devices are excluded. Paired school-work and leisure items asked over one multi-device scope are summed here as the two purpose parts, partial where the scope leaves out devices or the school part pools paid work; a pair on one device, or on the internet alone, follows that device's row or st_internet (DR-0002), and this row is incompatible. A leisure-only item with no paired school-work item (screen use for reasons other than school work) maps to st_leisure, and this row is incompatible ('Leisure only; see st_leisure'); a school-work-only item maps to st_educational, and this row is incompatible. A sum of separately asked activity or device items is incompatible, including a total the study computed from them (DR-0002, DR-0004). Internet-only and single-device items go to their own rows and are incompatible here. A skipped part leaves a summed total NA; never score it as zero unless the instrument's documentation does.

label: Screen Time: Watching (e.g., TV, streaming) on average weekday
description: Time spent watching content (e.g., TV, movies, streaming) on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_watch; rules as st_watch.

label: Screen Time: Watching (e.g., TV, streaming) on average weekend day
description: Time spent watching content (e.g., TV, movies, streaming) on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_watch; rules as st_watch.

label: Screen Time: Watching (e.g., TV, streaming) on usual day
description: Time spent watching content (e.g., TV, movies, streaming) on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: TV, films, series and online video on any device. Partial: an item limited to the TV set (broadcast TV, videos or DVDs on the set), or one that also counts gaming at the TV or radio. Viewing sources (broadcast, DVD, streaming, online video) may be summed here (DR-0002); record the sum. An item pooling watching with gaming, computer or internet use goes to st_total, or to st_leisure where it is restricted to leisure (reasons other than school work). An item on violent programmes or films only goes to st_violent_watch, and this row is incompatible ('Violent content only; see st_violent_watch'). An item on educational programmes or videos only goes to st_educontent_watch, and this row is incompatible ('Educational content only; see st_educontent_watch').

missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game; rules as st_game.

label: Screen Time: Gaming (any device) on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing video games on any device (console, computer, handheld, phone, tablet) on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game; rules as st_game.

label: Screen Time: Gaming (any device) on usual day
description: Time spent playing video games on any device (console, computer, handheld, phone, tablet) on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Device-specific gaming items may be summed here (DR-0002); record the sum. An item pooling gaming with other non-school computer use maps here as partial, and st_comp* is incompatible. An item whose examples name social media is not mapped here (incompatible). An item naming devices that leaves out phones and tablets (e.g. computer or console) is partial whatever its year; an item naming no device is compatible. An item on violent games only goes to st_violent_game, and this row is incompatible ('Violent games only; see st_violent_game').

label: Screen Time: Gaming on computer on average weekday
description: Time spent playing games on a computer on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_comp; rules as st_game_comp.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on computer on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing games on a computer on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game_comp; rules as st_game_comp.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on computer on usual day
description: Time spent playing games on a computer on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Computer gaming only. Computer and tablet offered as one response option go to st_game_tablet (partial); this row is then incompatible. Under a pooled multi-device gaming item this row is unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.').

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a regular console on average weekday
description: Time spent playing games on a regular console on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_console; rules as st_game_console.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a regular console on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing games on a regular console on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game_console; rules as st_game_console.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a regular console on usual day
description: Time spent playing games on a regular console on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Console gaming only. A console item that also covers handhelds maps here as partial, and st_game_handheldconsole is incompatible. Under a pooled multi-device gaming item this row is unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.').

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a handheld console on average weekday

notes: Not a preregistered content class. Generic row for a violent-viewing exposure index in the study's own metric, standardised within dataset at analysis: named titles (favourite or most-watched) each rated for violence (by the respondent, an official rating or the study's coding) and weighted by how often or how long each is watched, combined over titles (e.g. the mean of frequency x violence rating). The status reflects construct fit only: the rater and the time weight are recorded in st_violent_measure, and an index of TV programmes only is partial. Use a released index as released, keyed higher = more exposure, or build it from the items with the study's scoring where it is not released (e.g. a wave the study did not score); use it only where at least half of the titles the respondent answered about were rated (half-answered rule, titles as items; a title counts where any per-title answer, frequency, time or rating, is given; written names and title codes alone do not count). Where several versions qualify on one occasion (different time weights or raters), take a compatible version over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the others unused. Hours of violent viewing go to st_violent_watch, and this row is incompatible for them ('Hours of violent viewing; see st_violent_watch'). A study index pooled over viewing and gaming is not used; a combined score is derived at analysis from this row and st_violent_game_index. Incompatible, item named: violence ratings with no time or frequency weight (e.g. mean violence of favourite titles), frequency-only, preference or interest items, single items (including the share of viewing that is violent, e.g. most / some / none of it) and attitudes to media violence. label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - self-rated
description: Child-reported rating of their overall school performance, grades or class standing (their own view, or their teacher's view as they perceive it)
notes: The HBSC item (what the teacher thinks of the child's performance compared with classmates) or the child's own rating of overall grades or class standing. Five-level scales: the five-level collapse in the harmonisation guide (proximate). Letter or numeric grades go to acc_academachment_lettergrades or acc_academachment_numgrades; satisfaction with performance to wb_domainsat_schoolwork_self; parent ratings to acc_academachment_parentrated; academic self-concept scales to wb_selfconcept_academic_self, and subject self-concept items ('I am good at maths') to wb_selfconcept_maths_self, wb_selfconcept_verbal_self or wb_selfconcept_science_self. Quality-of-life school items (e.g. KIDSCREEN) and agreement- or truth-rated self-descriptions about school in general ('I am good at school work', 'I am clever') are incompatible, named; a scale of such self-descriptions goes to wb_selfconcept_academic_self.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - student grades (categorical letter grades)
description: Overall school grade reported as a letter grade
missing_rule: Use NA if not available; 'not graded', 'not sure' and pass/fail are NA
notes: Overall grade only; grades for single subjects are incompatible. Fold +/- onto the letter (proximate); 'Mostly X's' = X; a two-letter band = X/Y; an open bottom band ('D or lower') = D. Also map every letter-grade source to acc_academachment_numgrades, and never pool the two rows as independent outcomes.

label: Academic Achievement: General education - standardised tests
description: Score on a standardised general-education achievement test: an overall composite, or a subject other than reading and mathematics (e.g. science)
notes: Reading and mathematics tests go to acc_literacy_stdtest or acc_numeracy_stdtest, never here. Map one test per dataset (the one fielded in most waves) and record the test, domain and score type.

label: Academic Engagement: Cares about doing well in school
description: How often the child cares about doing well in school
notes: Frequency ratings only ('All/Most/Some of the time' = Always/Usually/Sometimes). Degree, importance or agreement ratings, effort items ('tries their best') and liking or enjoying school are incompatible; multi-item engagement or attitude-to-school scales go to acc_schoolengage_self (teacher-rated ones to acc_schoolengage_teacher). Record the informant and waves.

label: Academic Engagement: Completes all required homework
description: How often the child does all the homework they are required to do
notes: Completion-frequency items only. Homework time goes to acc_homework_time and is incompatible here; how often homework is set, parental checking, and difficulty or lateness items are incompatible. Record the informant and waves.

label: Academic Engagement: School engagement - engagement or attitude-to-school scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's multi-item scale of engagement with school or attitude to school and learning (effort, attention and participation in class, interest in and liking of school and learning), where higher indicates more engagement
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales of behavioural, emotional or cognitive engagement with school, or of attitude to school and learning (e.g. a school engagement scale, a school- or learning-attitude scale), a study's own scale included when the study released or documented its score, compatible. Disengagement and negative-attitude scales are reversed so higher = more engagement, and where a study releases engagement and disengagement scores separately, map engagement and name the other as unused. A scale that mixes attitude to school with feeling judged by teachers (e.g. the SENA Problems at School scale, reversed) is partial. A total that adds other facets (e.g. a school adjustment total with peer- or teacher-relationship subscales, or an engagement total with an academic-efficacy subscale) is partial, and its school-life, learning or engagement subscale, where released, is mapped before the total. A study's own items asked as one battery on engagement with no published or documented score (the mean of the items, complete-case), and class-preparedness batteries (coming to class without materials or without homework done), scored or not, are partial. Single items never fill this row: caring about doing well and completing homework stay on acc_schoolengage_caresschool and acc_schoolengage_homework, and liking or satisfaction items on wb_domainsat_school_self. Belonging and connectedness scales stay on acc_schoolbelonging_self (a study with both fills both), school-burnout and academic-stress scales go to acc_schoolstress_self, and academic self-efficacy and self-concept scales to wb_selfefficacy_academic_self and wb_selfconcept_academic_self; motivation-type, self-regulated learning, study-strategy and persistence scales (e.g. action-control or grit scales), test-anxiety and school-climate scales, and engagement or absorption scales not about school (e.g. the EPOCH engagement domain) are incompatible, named. Parent-rated scales are incompatible, named (no row holds them); teacher ratings go to acc_schoolengage_teacher and are incompatible here, named. Where two scales qualify on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the other as unused. Reverse negatively worded items so higher = more engagement; record the instrument in acc_schoolengage_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale changes. NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Academic Engagement: School engagement - engagement or school-adjustment scale (teacher report)
description: Score on a teacher-rated multi-item scale of the child's engagement with or adjustment to school and learning (taking part and making an effort in class, following class routines, interest in learning), where higher indicates more engagement
notes: Generic row for multi-item teacher-rated scales of the child's engagement with or adjustment to school and learning, rated by a school teacher or an early-childhood educator (preschool, kindergarten or child-care staff), a study's own scale included when the study released or documented its score, compatible; ratings by parents and family carers never fill this row. Classroom-engagement scales (participation, effort and attention in class) are engagement scales and compatible. A school adjustment total that adds peer- or teacher-relationship subscales is partial, and its school-life or learning subscale, where released, is mapped before the total. Behaviour-problem, attention and ADHD scales (beh_atten_teacher, beh_hyper_teacher, beh_adhdsymp_teacher), social-skills scales (beh_socialskills_teacher) and prosocial scales (beh_prosocial_teacher) stay on their teacher rows; scales presented as approaches to learning or work habits (mixing engagement with attentiveness, persistence or organisation) and teacher-child relationship scales have no row; all are incompatible here, named. Single teacher items and a study's own teacher items with no released or documented score never fill this row and are incompatible, named; self-ratings go to acc_schoolengage_self. Keyed higher = more engagement: reverse negatively worded items and scales of poor adjustment. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, applied to the teacher's ratings; where two scales qualify on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the other as unused. Where two teachers rated the child, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Record the instrument and rater in acc_schoolengage_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes. NA for children not enrolled in school, preschool or child care, or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Academic Engagement: School engagement measure
description: Source measure, informant, item count and scoring behind acc_schoolengage_self and acc_schoolengage_teacher
missing_rule: Should not be missing where acc_schoolengage_self or acc_schoolengage_teacher is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where neither scale was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: 'self: <instrument and subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; teacher: <instrument and subscale> (<rater: class or subject teacher, preschool or kindergarten teacher, or child-care staff>), <k> of <K> items, ...', naming only the rows mapped, then the reverse-scored items (or 'reversed as a whole'), the missing-item rule, which teacher rated where two could, and the added facets of any partial scale; one value per wave where the instruments change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See acc_schoolengage_self.') only when both score rows are unavailable or incompatible.

label: Academic Engagement: Time spent on homework
description: Time the child spends on homework or other self-study for school on an average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes that no homework is set or done
notes: Hours per average day under the screen-time band, Non-users and Day-of-use rules: minutes / 60; weekly totals / 7; 'none' = 0, closed bands at their midpoint, open top band at its stated lower bound (write it in notes); weekday and weekend items (5 x wd + 2 x we) / 7, a total for the whole weekend halved first (partial); hours on a day of homework x days with homework / 7 (partial); 0 where a filter item says no homework is set or done. Homework in and out of school, at home or elsewhere, is compatible. A study's homework total is used only where it follows these rules; where its codes flag a top-coded part instead of a value, sum the parts at their top codes. Self-study that also counts revision, exam preparation or work set by a private tutor or cram school is partial; time attending school lessons, tutoring or cram classes, or an item that counts it, is incompatible. An item on school days only is taken as the average day (partial); an item on yesterday or one named day is partial, and time-use diary minutes on a homework or study activity are summed per diary day and combined 5:2 over weekday and weekend diaries (partial). A homework item that names screens goes to st_educational; an item pooling homework with reading, hobbies or other activities is incompatible; completion frequency stays on acc_schoolengage_homework; a teacher's expected homework time for the class is incompatible. Any informant; where the child and a parent both report, use the child's; record the informant and waves. NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school. Values above 24 are kept and excluded at analysis.

label: Academic: Pressure from schoolwork (self-report)
description: How pressured the participant feels by the schoolwork they have to do
notes: Single item. Scales with other anchors map by rank and are proximate; record the anchors. A five-point pressure scale maps its top two levels to 'A lot'. Worry about school performance and test anxiety are related items (incompatible, item named). Multi-item academic-stress and school-burnout scales go to acc_schoolstress_self (a study with both fills both).

label: Academic: Academic stress - academic or school stress scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's multi-item scale of stress or strain from schoolwork, grades, homework and exams, or of school-burnout exhaustion, where higher indicates more academic stress
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales of academic or school-related stress (stress or strain from grades, homework, exams and school demands) and of school-burnout exhaustion, compatible. A school-burnout total that adds cynicism or inadequacy subscales, or reversed vigour items, is partial, and its exhaustion subscale, where released, is mapped before the total. A scale of how much school stressors affect the child that mixes relational or environmental stressors with academic ones is partial, and its academic subscale, where released, is mapped before the total, still partial; scales of how often stressors occur, without appraisal, and counts of school stressors are incompatible, named. The single pressure item stays on acc_schoolpressure_self, and a study with both fills both. Test-anxiety scales (no row holds them), general perceived-stress scales (mh_stress_scale_self), worry about the future, school-engagement and disengagement scales (acc_schoolengage_self) and academic self-efficacy scales (wb_selfefficacy_academic_self) never fill this row and are incompatible, named, as are single items. Parent- and teacher-rated scales are incompatible, named (no row holds them). Reverse positively worded items so higher = more stress; record the instrument in acc_schoolstress_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale changes. NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Academic: Academic stress measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind acc_schoolstress_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where acc_schoolstress_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the scale or items change. Status inferred.

label: Academic: School belonging (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's school belonging or connectedness scale, where higher indicates stronger belonging
notes: Generic row for multi-item belonging or connectedness scales. Reverse negatively worded items so higher = stronger belonging; record the instrument and scoring in acc_schoolbelonging_measure; standardise within dataset. Single items are incompatible; satisfaction with school goes to wb_domainsat_school_self. Only scales presented as belonging or connectedness; teacher- or classmate-support scales and school-environment quality-of-life subscales are incompatible, and engagement or attitude-to-school scales go to acc_schoolengage_self (a study with both fills both).

label: Academic: School belonging measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind acc_schoolbelonging_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where acc_schoolbelonging_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items. Status inferred.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - student grades (numeric)
description: Overall school grades on a numeric scale (grade points, percentage or national scale), including US letter grades converted to grade points, where higher indicates better achievement
notes: Reverse scales where a low mark is best (German 1-6: 7 - mark). US letter grades: A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0, +/- = ±0.3, two-letter bands at their midpoint, 'D or lower' = 1; one overall grade compatible, bands partial. Subject marks only: mean of all academic subjects reported (not arts, PE or ICT), all required, partial. Never convert between national scales; record the source metric.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - teacher-rated
description: Teacher's rating of the child's overall academic performance
notes: Teacher's overall rating, or the mean of the teacher's ratings of every academic subject rated (language, maths, science or social studies; not arts, PE or ICT), all required, partial; round half toward the poorer level. Five-level scales: the five-level collapse in the harmonisation guide. A student's report of the teacher's view goes to acc_academachment_selfrated, and a parent's rating to acc_academachment_parentrated.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - parent-rated
description: Parent or carer's rating of the child's overall school performance, grades or class standing
notes: Parent or carer's overall rating of the child's school work, grades or class standing, or the mean of the parent's ratings of every academic subject rated (language, maths, science or social studies; not arts, PE or ICT), all required, partial; round half toward the poorer level. Five-level scales: the five-level collapse in the harmonisation guide (proximate). Other scales map by label: excellent, very good or top of the class -> Very good; good or above average -> Good; average -> Average; every level below average -> Below average; a label not listed (e.g. fair, satisfactory) takes the level of its rank on the source scale, anchors in notes (proximate unless the source has exactly these four levels). Letter or numeric grades go to acc_academachment_lettergrades or acc_academachment_numgrades; satisfaction, effort and homework items are incompatible. NA for children not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Academic Achievement: Numeracy - standardised tests
description: Student performance on standardised numeracy or mathematics tests
notes: Record the test and score type in variables.csv; standardise within dataset and wave at analysis. BAS II Number Skills also maps to acc_numeracy_bas_numberskills.

label: Academic Achievement: Numeracy - British Ability Scales Number Skills
description: Standard score (mean 100, SD 15) on the BAS II Number Skills achievement scale
notes: Age-normed standard score; ability scores only as a partial fallback, since raw scores depend on the item set taken. The same score also maps to acc_numeracy_stdtest.

label: Academic Achievement: Literacy - standardised tests
description: Student performance on standardised literacy or reading tests
notes: Record the test and score type in variables.csv; standardise within dataset and wave at analysis. BAS II Word Reading also maps to acc_literacy_bas_wordreading.

label: Academic Achievement: Literacy - British Ability Scales Word Reading
description: Standard score (mean 100, SD 15) on the BAS II Word Reading achievement scale
notes: Age-normed standard score; ability scores only as a partial fallback, since raw scores depend on the item set taken. The same score also maps to acc_literacy_stdtest.

label: Academic: Learning disability - diagnosed
description: Whether a health professional has ever told the respondent the child has a specific learning disability (e.g. dyslexia or dyscalculia), and whether the child currently has it
notes: Never = never told; Previously = told, not current; Currently = told and current. Specific learning disability or disorder, such as dyslexia, dyscalculia or dysgraphia ('learning disability' in US usage); an item on one of these only (e.g. dyslexia), or an undefined 'learning difficulty', is partial. A binary ever-told item: told = Currently, not told = Never (partial); it does not fill waves of a row whose other waves separate current from previous diagnosis, which stay NA. Where a wave skips children already reported told of the condition at an earlier interview, a skipped child whose latest earlier answer was told takes Currently (partial), and the notes name the routing. Treatment, or being told within a recent recall window, as proxy for current: partial. Intellectual disability ('learning disability' in UK usage), developmental delay and ADHD do not map here. Not attributed to a health professional (e.g. a school special-needs category or IEP): incompatible. A stem that pools educators with health professionals ('a doctor, other health care provider, or educator ever told you') counts as attributed to a health professional, with no loss of status. Not an achievement score; never pool with the grade or test rows. Record the informant.

label: Academic: Learning disability - diagnosed severity
description: Respondent-rated severity of the child's current learning disability
notes: Use NA where the child is not currently diagnosed; pairs with acc_learningdisab_diagnosed. Ratings of how much a condition affects learning or daily activities are incompatible.

label: Academic: Grade retention - ever repeated a school year
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant has ever repeated (been held back in) a grade or school year
notes: TRUE if the participant has ever repeated (been held back in) a grade or school year of primary or secondary school, FALSE if never. Repeating kindergarten counts where kindergarten is the first compulsory school year or the first year of the school system (e.g. US kindergarten); repeating a pre-school or nursery year does not. Items on separate school stages combine: TRUE if any is TRUE, FALSE only if all are FALSE; an item on one stage only (e.g. repeated a year in secondary school) is partial unless other items cover the other stages. A released count of grades repeated is TRUE above 0. An undefined 'school failure' item and an item on repeating within a recall window (e.g. since the last interview) are partial. Delayed school entry and dropping out of school are not retention and are incompatible, named. Any informant (the child, a parent or school records), recorded; where two informants report on one occasion, use the screen-time respondent's report and name the other as unused. Within participant, an observed TRUE is carried to every later wave the participant attended, over a later FALSE too (filled in the tidier), and a carried TRUE keeps the row's status; a FALSE is never carried, forward or backward. NA for children not yet enrolled in school.

label: Behaviour: Hyperactivity - Behavior Assessment System for Children-2 Hyperactivity subscale
description: Raw score on the BASC-2 Parent Rating Scales Hyperactivity scale, where higher indicates more hyperactivity
notes: Raw score, not the T-score. Record the form (PRS-P, PRS-C, PRS-A), items answered of the scale total and the observed range. When mapped, repeat its expression on beh_hyper_parent. Studies without the BASC-2: unavailable, pointing to the row that holds the study's hyperactivity scale (e.g. beh_hyper_parent, beh_adhdsymp_parent or beh_hyper_sdq_parent).

label: Behaviour: Attention - Behavior Assessment System for Children-2 Attention subscale
description: Raw score on the BASC-2 Parent Rating Scales Attention Problems scale, where higher indicates more attention problems
notes: Raw score, not the T-score. Record the form, items answered of the scale total and the observed range. When mapped, repeat its expression on beh_atten_parent. Studies without the BASC-2: unavailable, pointing to the row that holds the study's attention scale (e.g. beh_atten_parent, beh_adhdsymp_parent or beh_hyper_sdq_parent).

label: Behaviour: Attention - inattention scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported inattention or concentration-problems scale, without hyperactivity-impulsivity items, where higher indicates more inattention
notes: Multi-item self-report scale of inattention or concentration problems without hyperactivity-impulsivity items; say in beh_atten_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. Single items and item subsets of broader instruments are incompatible, named in source_columns, with a pointer to any row that holds them (e.g. beh_hyper_sdq_*). Attentional subscales of impulsivity scales (e.g. the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale attentional subscale) stay with their total on beh_impulsivity_self. A scale that mixes inattention with hyperactivity-impulsivity items, and a combined ADHD total, go to beh_adhdsymp_self, and hyperactivity-impulsivity scales to beh_hyper_self; with no inattention-only scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Parent- or carer-rated inattention and ADHD scales go to beh_atten_parent or beh_adhdsymp_parent, and teacher-rated attention and ADHD scales to beh_atten_teacher, beh_hyper_teacher or beh_adhdsymp_teacher; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them.

label: Behaviour: Hyperactivity-Impulsivity - hyperactivity-impulsivity scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported hyperactivity or hyperactivity-impulsivity scale or subscale, where higher indicates more hyperactivity and impulsivity
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and subscales of hyperactivity or hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms without inattention items (e.g. the hyperactivity-impulsivity subscale of an ADHD self-report screen such as the UMass ADHD self-report, the SENA hyperactivity-impulsivity scale, the Conners 3 self-report hyperactivity/impulsivity scale), compatible; an impulsivity-symptom-only subscale is partial. A scale that mixes hyperactivity-impulsivity with inattention items, and a combined ADHD total, go to beh_adhdsymp_self; with no hyperactivity-impulsivity scale free of inattention items in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. SDQ hyperactivity/inattention stays on beh_hyper_sdq_self and is incompatible here, named. Trait impulsivity scales stay on beh_impulsivity_self and are incompatible here, named; temperament activity-level scales and single items are incompatible, named. Where two qualifying scales were given on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, naming the other as unused. Parent- or carer-rated hyperactivity scales go to beh_hyper_parent and teacher-rated ones to beh_hyper_teacher; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Record the instrument in beh_atten_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: ADHD Symptoms - combined ADHD symptom scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale that combines inattention with hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms, or a released combined ADHD total, where higher indicates more ADHD symptoms
notes: Generic row for self-report scales that mix inattention with hyperactivity-impulsivity items and release no separate inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores (e.g. the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale screener, the Youth Self-Report DSM-oriented Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Problems scale, a study's attention-hyperactivity scale with no subscale key), and for a released combined ADHD total or index that is not the sum or mean of scores mapped on beh_atten_self and beh_hyper_self, compatible. A scale that adds off-construct items is partial. A released combined total that is the sum or mean of an instrument's inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity subscales maps here only when those subscales are not released or scorable; where they are mapped and no other qualifying scale is in hand, this row is unavailable ('Derive at analysis from beh_atten_self, beh_hyper_self.'). For the Youth Self-Report, map the DSM-oriented scale where it can be scored and name the Attention Problems syndrome as unused. Where two qualifying scales were given on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, naming the other as unused. SDQ hyperactivity/inattention stays on beh_hyper_sdq_self and is incompatible here, named; trait impulsivity scales stay on beh_impulsivity_self. Parent- or carer-rated ADHD scales go to beh_adhdsymp_parent and teacher-rated ones to beh_adhdsymp_teacher; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Record the instrument in beh_atten_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Attention and ADHD symptom measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_atten_self, beh_hyper_self and beh_adhdsymp_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_atten_self, beh_hyper_self or beh_adhdsymp_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>' for the one score row mapped; where two or three of beh_atten_self, beh_hyper_self and beh_adhdsymp_self are mapped, one such segment per row, prefixed 'attention: ', 'hyperactivity-impulsivity: ' and 'combined ADHD: ', naming each instrument; then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred; unavailable ('See beh_atten_self.') only when all three score rows are unavailable or incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Attention - single item (teacher report)
description: Teacher's single-item rating of the child's attention in class, where higher indicates more attention problems
notes: One global teacher rating of how attentive the child is in class (e.g. how often the student is attentive in your class, pays attention or concentrates), rated by frequency or degree; an item on one facet (listens to instructions, stays on task) is partial. Reverse attentiveness wording so higher = more attention problems, the direction of the other beh_atten_* rows; record the scale points, anchors and recall period (a rating of the child in the teacher's current class needs no other window); standardise within dataset. Where two teachers rated the same item, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Items and scores of truth-rated checklists (SDQ, TRF) and of other multi-item teacher scales are incompatible here: multi-item teacher inattention, hyperactivity and ADHD scales go to beh_atten_teacher, beh_hyper_teacher or beh_adhdsymp_teacher, and the SDQ teacher hyperactivity/inattention subscale stays on beh_hyper_sdq_teacher. A yes/no teacher flag (e.g. 'appears hyperactive') and a self- or parent-rated item, including a report of teachers' complaints, are incompatible, item named.

label: Behaviour: Impulsivity - impulsivity scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's self-reported impulsivity scale, where higher indicates more impulsivity
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales presented as impulsivity or impulsiveness (e.g. the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale BIS-11, BIS-Brief or BIS-15, Eysenck Impulsiveness, the Dolejs and Skopal impulsivity scale) or a published impulsivity subscale of a broader instrument; say in beh_impulsivity_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. Released subscales that together make up a published total are summed to that total. A score that mixes in sensation-seeking, thrill-seeking or irresponsibility items (e.g. UPPS-P total, YPI impulsive-irresponsible) is partial. Incompatible, named: single items, parent- or teacher-rated scales (parent-rated hyperactivity-impulsivity and ADHD scales go to beh_hyper_parent or beh_adhdsymp_parent), sensation seeking alone, self-control and effortful-control scales, and ADHD or hyperactivity-impulsivity symptom scales and their subscales (self-report ones go to beh_atten_self, beh_hyper_self or beh_adhdsymp_self). The score and its subscales do not also map to beh_atten_self, beh_ext_self or the aggression rows (beh_agg_self, beh_aggphys_self, beh_aggrel_self); inhibitory-control tasks go to cog_inhib_task, and delay-discounting and other choice tasks map to no row. Self-report self-control and effortful-control scales go to beh_selfreg_self, and parent- or carer-rated ones to beh_selfreg_parent. Standardise within dataset.

label: Behaviour: Impulsivity measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_impulsivity_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_impulsivity_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscales>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Self-regulation - Head-Toes-Knees-Shoulders
description: Total score on the Head-Toes-Knees-Shoulders task (direct assessment), where higher indicates better behavioural self-regulation
notes: Sum of item scores (0 incorrect, 1 self-corrected, 2 correct). Record the item count and total range (e.g. 30 items, 0-60). Parent- or carer-rated self-regulation scales go to beh_selfreg_parent and self-report self-control scales to beh_selfreg_self; neither pools with this task.

label: Behaviour: Self-regulation - self-regulation or self-control scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale of the child's behavioural self-regulation (self-control, inhibitory or effortful control), where higher indicates more self-regulation
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of self-control or behavioural self-regulation: controlling impulses, waiting, stopping or switching an activity when asked, following rules without reminders, keeping at a task (e.g. the self-control subscale of a parent social skills rating scale), compatible. Temperament effortful-control scales (e.g. the Children's Behavior Questionnaire or Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire, any form) are partial: map the broad effortful-control score where released or scorable from the form's effortful-control items (a study's mean of its effortful-control subscales counts), else the inhibitory-control subscale, and name the others as unused; temperament negative-affect and anger/frustration scales go to beh_temp_negaffect_parent and activity, approach, impulsivity and surgency scales to beh_temp_surgency_parent; they and temperament attentional-focusing scales never map here. A scale that joins self-regulation with another facet (e.g. independence or autonomy items with task persistence) is partial. An executive-function questionnaire other than the BRIEF and BASC-2 (e.g. the Early Executive Functions Questionnaire) gives its inhibitory-control subscale here, partial, and its total to cog_execfunc_parent; the BRIEF and the BASC-2 executive-functioning scale, with their scales and indexes, stay on their own rows and are incompatible here, named. Head-Toes-Knees-Shoulders and inhibitory-control tasks stay on beh_selfreg_htks and cog_inhib_task and are incompatible here, named. Hyperactivity-impulsivity, attention-problem, oppositional and other problem scales, SDQ and CBCL scores included, never map here; with only those in hand the row is incompatible, naming them and the rows that hold them. Emotion dysregulation scales go to beh_emotdysreg_parent and emotion regulation competence scales to beh_emotreg_parent. Self-report self-control scales go to beh_selfreg_self and never pool here. Single items, study checklists with no published scoring and teacher or examiner ratings are incompatible, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more self-regulation (reverse a scale of poor self-control); record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave or age group where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Emotion dysregulation - emotion dysregulation scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale of the child's emotion dysregulation (emotional lability, negativity or poor emotional self-control), where higher indicates more emotion dysregulation
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of emotional lability, negativity or poor emotional self-control: mood swings, quick or intense frustration, over-excitement, being slow to calm down (e.g. the Emotion Regulation Checklist lability/negativity subscale, an emotional dysregulation subscale), compatible. When wb_emotsc_basc2 is mapped, repeat its expression here. Regulation-competence scales keyed the other way (e.g. the Emotion Regulation Checklist emotion regulation subscale of emotional awareness, empathy and appropriate affect) go to beh_emotreg_parent: they are incompatible here, named, and are never reversed onto this row, and a study with both kinds fills both rows. Anger or irritability mood scales, temperament negative-affect or anger-frustration scales (beh_temp_negaffect_parent), single-emotion scales (anger, sadness, fear) and the CBCL emotionally reactive syndrome (mh_emotreact_cbcl_parent) are incompatible, named; other SDQ and CBCL scores never map here. The BRIEF emotional-control scale stays with the BRIEF and is incompatible here, named. Oppositional, conduct, hyperactivity and other problem scales never map here; with only those in hand the row is incompatible, naming them and the rows that hold them. Self-report dysregulation scales go to beh_emotdysreg_self and never pool here. Single items, study checklists with no published scoring and teacher or examiner ratings are incompatible, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more dysregulation; record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave or age group where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Emotion regulation - emotion regulation competence scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale of the child's emotion regulation competence (expressing emotions appropriately, saying how they feel, empathy, recovering from upset), where higher indicates better emotion regulation
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of the child's emotion regulation competence: expressing emotions appropriately, being able to say how they feel, empathy, recovering quickly from upset, calming down (e.g. the Emotion Regulation Checklist emotion regulation subscale), compatible. A regulation scale of a broader behaviour or social-emotional questionnaire that pools emotional with behavioural regulation is partial. Executive-function questionnaires never fill this row: their regulation and emotional-control scales (e.g. the BRIEF emotional-control scale, the regulation scale of an early executive functions questionnaire) are incompatible, named, and only an inhibitory-control subscale of an executive-function questionnaire other than the BRIEF and BASC-2 maps, to beh_selfreg_parent, and such a questionnaire's total goes to cog_execfunc_parent. Dysregulation scales (e.g. the Emotion Regulation Checklist lability/negativity subscale, the BASC-2 emotional self-control scale, an emotional dysregulation subscale) go to beh_emotdysreg_parent and are never reversed onto this row; a study with both kinds fills both rows. Anger or irritability mood scales, temperament scales (soothability included), resilience and adaptive-skills scales (e.g. the BASC-2 resiliency scale), social-skills self-control subscales (beh_selfreg_parent), prosocial scales (beh_prosocial_parent) and empathy-only scales (no parent row holds them) are incompatible, named. Oppositional, conduct, hyperactivity and other problem scales, SDQ and CBCL scores included, never map here; with only those or dysregulation scales in hand the row is incompatible, naming them and the rows that hold them. Single items (a stays-calm frequency item goes to beh_emotreg_stayscalm), study checklists with no published scoring and teacher or examiner ratings are incompatible, named, and a parent's own emotion regulation never fills this row. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = better regulation; record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave or age group where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Self-regulation - self-control or self-regulation scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale of self-control or self-regulation (resisting temptation and impulses, self-discipline, controlling one's temper and reactions), where higher indicates more self-control
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and published subscales presented as self-control or self-regulation: resisting temptation and impulses, breaking bad habits, self-discipline, delaying gratification, controlling one's temper and reactions (e.g. the Brief Self-Control Scale or a documented short form of it, the self-control subscale of a student social skills rating form), compatible, in any rating format; say in beh_selfreg_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. A scale that joins self-control with another facet (e.g. a self-control subscale that adds problem-solving or stress-coping items) is partial. Reverse a scale presented as low behavioural self-control (a scale presented as poor emotional self-control is a dysregulation scale, beh_emotdysreg_self); anger and anger-control-problem scales (e.g. the Buss-Perry anger subscale; beh_anger_self), hostility and irritability scales and emotion dysregulation scales (beh_emotdysreg_self) are problem scales, are never reversed onto this row and are incompatible, named. Self-report temperament effortful-control scales are partial: the broad effortful-control score where released or scorable, else the inhibitory-control subscale; other temperament scales never map here. An executive-function questionnaire other than the BRIEF and BASC-2 gives its inhibitory-control subscale here, partial, and its total to cog_execfunc_self; the BRIEF and BASC-2 executive-function scales, any form, never fill this row and are incompatible, named. Incompatible, named: scales presented as impulsivity and their subscales (beh_impulsivity_self), inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity and ADHD symptom scales (beh_atten_self, beh_hyper_self, beh_adhdsymp_self), grit, perseverance and conscientiousness scales, emotion regulation, strategy and emotional awareness scales (beh_emotreg_self, beh_emotreg_suppression_self, beh_emotreg_reappraisal_self, beh_emotaware_self), Head-Toes-Knees-Shoulders and inhibitory-control tasks (beh_selfreg_htks, cog_inhib_task), single items (a stays-calm frequency item goes to beh_emotreg_stayscalm) and study checklists with no published scoring. Conduct, hyperactivity and other problem scales, SDQ scores included, never map here; with only those in hand the row is incompatible, naming them and the rows that hold them. Parent- or carer-rated self-regulation scales go to beh_selfreg_parent and never pool here; teacher and examiner ratings do not map. Keyed higher = more self-control; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Emotion regulation - emotion regulation scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale of emotion regulation ability (managing, calming or recovering from negative emotions and keeping a positive mood), where higher indicates better emotion regulation
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and published subscales presented as emotion regulation or emotion management: managing and regulating one's emotions, calming down, recovering from upset, keeping a good mood when something bad happens (e.g. the manage-and-regulate scale of an emotional skills and competence questionnaire), compatible, in any rating format; say in beh_selfreg_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. Strategy scales go to their own rows (expressive suppression to beh_emotreg_suppression_self, cognitive reappraisal to beh_emotreg_reappraisal_self); they are incompatible here, named, and are never combined into a regulation score. Scales presented as self-control, temper or anger control included, go to beh_selfreg_self, and emotional awareness or clarity scales go to beh_emotaware_self. Dysregulation-keyed scales and totals (e.g. the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale, an emotional regulation problems subscale) go to beh_emotdysreg_self: they are incompatible here, named, and are never reversed onto this row, and a study with both kinds fills both rows. Anger, hostility or irritability scales, personality emotional-stability or neuroticism scales and global trait emotional intelligence totals are incompatible, named. Single items (a stays-calm frequency item goes to beh_emotreg_stayscalm) and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Oppositional, conduct, hyperactivity and other problem scales, SDQ scores included, never map here; with only those or dysregulation scales in hand the row is incompatible, naming them and the rows that hold them. Parent- or carer-rated regulation scales go to beh_emotreg_parent and never pool here. Keyed higher = better regulation; standardise within dataset.

label: Behaviour: Emotion dysregulation - emotion dysregulation scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale of emotion dysregulation (difficulties regulating emotions, emotional lability or poor emotional self-control), where higher indicates more emotion dysregulation
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and published subscales of emotion dysregulation: difficulties regulating or recovering from negative emotions, emotional lability, mood swings, quick or intense frustration, losing control when upset (e.g. the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale or a documented short form of it, an emotional regulation problems subscale), compatible, in any rating format; say in beh_selfreg_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. Competence-keyed regulation scales go to beh_emotreg_self: they are incompatible here, named, and are never reversed onto this row, and a study with both kinds fills both rows. Strategy scales (beh_emotreg_suppression_self, beh_emotreg_reappraisal_self), emotional awareness scales (beh_emotaware_self) and self-control scales (beh_selfreg_self), including a scale presented as low behavioural self-control, which is reversed there, are incompatible here, named. Anger or irritability mood scales, anger-control-problem scales (anger scales go to beh_anger_self), single-emotion scales (anger, sadness, fear), temperament negative-affect scales and personality emotional-stability or neuroticism scales are incompatible, named. The BRIEF emotional-control scale, any form, stays with the BRIEF and is incompatible here, named. Oppositional, conduct, hyperactivity and other problem scales, SDQ scores included, never map here; with only those in hand the row is incompatible, naming them and the rows that hold them. Single items and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named, and a parent's own emotion regulation never fills this row. Parent- or carer-rated dysregulation scales go to beh_emotdysreg_parent and never pool here; teacher and examiner ratings do not map. Keyed higher = more dysregulation; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Emotion regulation - expressive suppression scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported expressive suppression scale (regulating emotions by not showing them), where higher indicates more use of expressive suppression
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales of expressive suppression as an emotion regulation strategy (e.g. the suppression subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire or of its child and adolescent version, ERQ-CA), compatible in any rating format, with the scale points and any change from the published form recorded in beh_selfreg_measure; score the mean of the items, as the instrument does. Keyed higher = more suppression: the row records how much the strategy is used, not how well emotions are regulated, so it is never reversed, never combined with reappraisal into one score and never pooled with beh_emotreg_self or beh_emotdysreg_self. Emotion inhibition or hiding subscales of other emotion-management instruments are partial. Single items and study item sets with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Parent-rated forms are incompatible, named, and a parent's own suppression items never fill this row. Standardise within dataset.

label: Behaviour: Emotion regulation - cognitive reappraisal scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported cognitive reappraisal scale (regulating emotions by changing how one thinks about a situation), where higher indicates more use of cognitive reappraisal
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales of cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy (e.g. the reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire or ERQ-CA), compatible in any rating format, with the scale points and any change from the published form recorded in beh_selfreg_measure; score the mean of the items, as the instrument does. A reappraisal subscale of another coping or strategy inventory (e.g. the positive reappraisal scale of a cognitive emotion regulation questionnaire) is partial. Keyed higher = more reappraisal; never combined with suppression into one score and never pooled with beh_emotreg_self or beh_emotdysreg_self. Single items and study item sets with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Parent-rated forms are incompatible, named, and a parent's own reappraisal items never fill this row. Standardise within dataset.

label: Behaviour: Emotional awareness - emotional awareness scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale of awareness of one's own emotions (recognising, understanding and naming one's feelings), where higher indicates more emotional awareness
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and published subscales of awareness and clarity of one's own emotions: knowing what one feels and why, noticing changes in one's mood, being able to tell and name one's feelings (e.g. the emotional awareness subscale of a personal strengths inventory), compatible, in any rating format; say in beh_selfreg_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. A subscale that pools awareness of one's own emotions with expressing them is partial. Difficulties-keyed awareness or clarity scales (e.g. the awareness and clarity subscales of the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale, alexithymia scales) are incompatible, named, and are never reversed onto this row. Scales of perceiving other people's emotions, empathy scales (beh_empathy_self) and emotion regulation, strategy or self-control scales are incompatible here, named, with a pointer to any row that holds them. Single items and study item sets with no published scoring are incompatible, named; parent-rated scales never fill this row. Keyed higher = more awareness; standardise within dataset.

label: Behaviour: Self-report self-regulation and emotion measure
description: Source instrument, item counts and item scoring behind the self-report self-regulation and emotion rows (beh_selfreg_self, beh_emotreg_self, beh_emotdysreg_self, beh_emotreg_suppression_self, beh_emotreg_reappraisal_self and beh_emotaware_self)
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any of beh_selfreg_self, beh_emotreg_self, beh_emotdysreg_self, beh_emotreg_suppression_self, beh_emotreg_reappraisal_self or beh_emotaware_self is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument> (self-report); self-control: <scale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; emotion regulation: ...; emotion dysregulation: ...; suppression: ...; reappraisal: ...; emotional awareness: ...', naming only the rows mapped and each instrument where rows draw on different ones, then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the missing-item rule, and any change of response format, item set or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the instruments or items change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See beh_selfreg_self.') only when every row it describes is unavailable or incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Temperament - negative affectivity scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated temperament scale of the child's negative affectivity (proneness to anger, frustration, fear, sadness and distress, and slow soothing), where higher indicates more negative affectivity
notes: Generic row for the broad negative-affectivity factor of a parent- or carer-rated temperament questionnaire (e.g. the Negative Affectivity scale of the Infant Behavior Questionnaire-Revised, Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire or Children's Behavior Questionnaire, any form), compatible; where the form releases facets only, the mean of all the form's negative-affect facets counts as the broad score (compatible). The mean of some of those facets, a single facet (e.g. anger/frustration, distress to limitations, fear, sadness), a study composite that adds other items to negative affect (e.g. reversed smiling and laughter), and the emotionality, irritability or negative-mood scale of another temperament instrument (e.g. EAS or EASI emotionality, an infant irritability scale) are partial. Effortful-control scales stay on beh_selfreg_parent and surgency scales go to beh_temp_surgency_parent; orienting and regulation scales (e.g. duration of orienting), cooperativeness or manageability scales, 'difficult child' ratings, infant regulatory-problem checklists, single items and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Emotion dysregulation scales stay on beh_emotdysreg_parent, anger or irritability mood scales that are not temperament scales fill no parent row, and problem scales (SDQ, CBCL including emotionally reactive, internalising) stay on their rows; none of them pools here, and this row never fills them. Teacher and self ratings are incompatible, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide (the raw mean or sum the instrument defines), keyed higher = more negative affectivity; a score averaged over two parents' ratings is partial. Where two scales qualify on one occasion, map compatible over partial, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the other as unused. Record the instrument, form and scales in beh_temp_measure; standardise within dataset, and within form or age band where the instrument changes with age.
