label: Behaviour: Temperament - surgency or extraversion scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated temperament scale of the child's surgency or extraversion (activity, approach, high-intensity pleasure, impulsivity and sociability), where higher indicates more surgency
notes: Generic row for the broad surgency or extraversion factor of a parent- or carer-rated temperament questionnaire (e.g. the Surgency scale of the IBQ-R, ECBQ or CBQ, any form), compatible; where the form releases facets only, the mean of all the form's surgency facets (shyness reversed where the form puts it in the factor) counts as the broad score (compatible). The mean of some of those facets, a single facet (e.g. activity level, approach, high-intensity pleasure, impulsivity, sociability) and the activity, sociability or approach scale of another temperament instrument (e.g. EAS or EASI activity or sociability, an infant approach-sociability scale) are partial. A shyness scale on its own (e.g. EAS shyness) is named as unused and never reversed onto this row. Hyperactivity-impulsivity and ADHD symptom scales stay on their rows (beh_hyper_parent, beh_adhdsymp_parent), negative-affect scales go to beh_temp_negaffect_parent and effortful-control scales stay on beh_selfreg_parent; orienting, cooperativeness or manageability scales, single items and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Teacher and self ratings are incompatible, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more surgency (reverse a withdrawal-keyed approach scale); a score averaged over two parents' ratings is partial. Where two scales qualify on one occasion, map compatible over partial, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the other as unused. Record the instrument, form and scales in beh_temp_measure; standardise within dataset, and within form or age band where the instrument changes with age.

label: Behaviour: Temperament measure
description: Source instrument, form, informant, item counts and item scoring behind beh_temp_negaffect_parent and beh_temp_surgency_parent
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_temp_negaffect_parent or beh_temp_surgency_parent is non-missing; NA in waves where neither was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and form> (<informant>); negative affectivity: <scale or facets>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; surgency: ...', naming only the rows mapped, then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the facets averaged where no broad score is released, the off-construct items of a partial composite, any averaging over two parents' ratings and the forms by age where the instrument changes with age; one value per wave where the instruments or forms change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See beh_temp_negaffect_parent.') only when both score rows are unavailable or incompatible. Temperament effortful control stays on beh_selfreg_parent and is recorded in beh_parent_measure.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Engaged in bullying other students
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports bullying other students during the study's recall period
notes: Bullying other students, in person or in a mode the item leaves open; where the study asks the mode, use the in-person answer. Online-only items go to beh_bullied_online. Compatible: a global bullying item or a multi-type perpetration checklist. Partial: hurtful acts not framed as bullying, a target wider than peers, or parent report. Truth-rated items (SDQ item 12, CBCL) are incompatible; name the item.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Bullied by other students
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports being bullied by other students during the study's recall period
notes: Compatible: a global bullying item, or any item of a multi-type peer-victimisation checklist (hit, threatened, teased, left out, rumours, belongings taken or damaged, extortion). Online-only items go to beh_beenbullied_online and stay out of the checklist; where the study asks the mode, use the in-person answer. Partial: hurtful acts not framed as bullying, any perpetrator rather than peers, or parent report. Truth-rated items (SDQ item 19, CBCL) are incompatible; name the item. Teacher-rated victimisation scales go to beh_victphys_teacher, beh_victrel_teacher or beh_vict_teacher and are incompatible here, named.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Bullied online by others
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports being bullied online
notes: Online or electronic bullying by anyone; peer-only items are compatible. Compatible: a global cyberbullying item or a multi-type checklist of cyberbullying acts (abuse, rumours, exclusion, exposing personal information, threats, extortion). Partial: an item on one act type, or a single hostile or humiliating experience not framed as bullying.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Bullied others online
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports bullying others online during the study's recall period
notes: Online or electronic bullying of anyone. Compatible: a global item or a multi-type checklist of cyberbullying acts. Partial: an item on one act type, or hostile acts not framed as bullying.

label: Behaviour: Fighting - Engaged in fighting
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports being in a physical fight during the study's recall period
notes: Partial: an item limited to one setting (school property; school or work) or form (group fights), or one counting any push or hit. Truth-rated items ('I fight a lot', SDQ 12, CBCL 'gets in many fights') are incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Truancy - Missed school without permission
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports missing school without permission during the study's recall period
notes: Unexcused absence from school or classes (truancy, skipping, cutting), whole or part days; whole-day-only items are compatible. Absence through illness or with permission does not count. TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period. NA for respondents not enrolled in school.

label: Behaviour: Suspension - Suspended or excluded from school
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant was suspended or excluded from school during the study's recall period
notes: Out-of-school suspension or exclusion from school for behaviour, fixed-term or permanent (expulsion counts), reported by the participant, a parent or carer, or school records (e.g. transcribed by a teacher), all compatible; a count of suspensions or of days suspended is TRUE above 0. TRUE for any occurrence, FALSE for none; a set of suspension and expulsion items follows the multi-item composite rule. Where two or more informants report on one occasion, use a compatible report over a partial one, then the screen-time respondent's report, as for acc_graderepeated, and name the others as unused; never coalesce informants. Partial: in-school suspension only, expulsion only, an item pooling suspension with probation or other disciplinary action, and lifetime or 'ever' items. Where an out-of-school suspension item (alone or pooled with probation or other disciplinary action) is in hand, in-school suspension items are named as unused and never added. Incompatible, named: disciplinary problems or trouble at school not framed as suspension, detention, being sent to the principal, parents called in about behaviour, a required change of school or disciplinary transfer, and suspension given only as a reason for not being enrolled. Record the informant, the items and the recall period. NA for respondents not enrolled in school.

label: Behaviour: Stealing - Took money or property without permission
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports stealing money or property during the study's recall period
notes: Theft of money or property: shoplifting; theft from a person, home, school or vehicle; vehicle theft; burglary; card use without permission. Shoplifting only: partial. Not here: extortion (bullying rows), fare evasion, driving without permission, steal-or-damage items, truth-rated SDQ items. TRUE at any occurrence; record each wave's items and recall period.

label: Behaviour: Vandalism - Deliberately damaged property
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports deliberately damaging or destroying property that was not theirs during the study's recall period
notes: Deliberate damage to others' property: breaking, graffiti, setting fire to property. One setting only (school property): partial. Not here: fire-setting with no property named, neighbourhood vandalism. TRUE at any occurrence; record each wave's items and recall period.

label: Behaviour: Alcohol use (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports drinking alcohol during the study's recall period
notes: Any drinking; items on drunkenness or binge drinking only are partial. TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period (past 30 days preferred). Lifetime items are partial.

label: Behaviour: Tobacco use (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports smoking tobacco during the study's recall period
notes: Cigarettes or other smoked tobacco. Items on e-cigarettes or vaping alone go to beh_vaping_self and are incompatible here; items pooling them with smoked tobacco are partial here and on beh_vaping_self. TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period. Lifetime items are partial.

label: Behaviour: E-cigarette use (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports using an e-cigarette or other vaping device during the study's recall period
notes: E-cigarettes, vape pens and pods, whatever the content (nicotine, nicotine-free, cannabis or unknown): TRUE for any occurrence and FALSE for none, from one item or any answered item of a set asked by content (multi-item composite rule); record the recall period (past 30 days preferred) and the contents asked. Partial: lifetime items, items asking only nicotine vaping or only cannabis vaping, and items pooling vaping with smoked tobacco (also partial on beh_tobacco_self). Incompatible, named: heated tobacco, smokeless tobacco and nicotine pouches, nicotine replacement, other people's vaping (e.g. vaping in the home), and susceptibility, curiosity or intention items. Use self-report; a parent-reported item is partial.

label: Behaviour: Cannabis use (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports using cannabis during the study's recall period
notes: TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period. Lifetime items are partial; items pooling cannabis with other drugs are partial here and on beh_drugs_self, which takes illicit drugs other than cannabis.

label: Behaviour: Other illicit drug use (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports using an illicit drug other than cannabis during the study's recall period
notes: Any illicit drug other than cannabis (e.g. amphetamines or methamphetamine, MDMA, cocaine, heroin, hallucinogens, ketamine, synthetic cannabinoids or other new psychoactive substances, and inhalants or solvents sniffed to get high): TRUE if any answered item is positive, FALSE if every answered item is never, NA if none is answered (multi-item composite rule), and a gate item answered never (e.g. never used any illegal drug or inhalant) makes every follow-up never; record the drugs asked and the recall period. Partial: lifetime items, a checklist that asks only one or two drugs or omits most drug classes, and items pooling cannabis with other drugs (also partial on beh_cannabis_self). Incompatible, named: non-medical use of prescription or over-the-counter medicines (e.g. tranquillisers, sedatives, stimulants, opioid painkillers, cough medicine), anabolic steroids, an item pooling illicit drugs with either of them, a fictitious drug included to detect over-reporting, alcohol, tobacco, vaping and cannabis items (their own rows), prescribed medication taken as directed, and attitude, availability, offer or intention items. Use self-report; a parent-reported item is partial.

label: Behaviour: Conduct Problems - Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire Conduct Problems subscale (parent/carer report)
description: Subscale score using standard 0-2 item scoring
notes: Items 5, 7r, 12, 18, 22 (r = reversed); the 2-4 form's substitutes for items 18 and 22 score the same. Score by the SDQ rule in the harmonisation guide.

label: Behaviour: Hyperactivity/Inattention - Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire Hyperactivity subscale (parent/carer report)
description: Subscale score using standard 0-2 item scoring
notes: Items 2, 10, 15, 21r, 25r (r = reversed); the 2-4 form's rewording of item 21 scores the same. Score by the SDQ rule in the harmonisation guide.

label: Behaviour: Peer Relationship Problems - Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire Peer Problems subscale (parent/carer report)
description: Subscale score using standard 0-2 item scoring
notes: Items 6, 11r, 14r, 19, 23 (r = reversed). Score by the SDQ rule in the harmonisation guide.

label: Behaviour: Prosocial Behaviour - Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire Prosocial subscale (parent/carer report)
description: Subscale score using standard 0-2 item scoring
notes: Items 1, 4, 9, 17, 20; none reversed. Score by the SDQ rule in the harmonisation guide. When mapped, repeat its expression on beh_prosocial_parent.

label: Behaviour: Physical Aggression - Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire Short Form Physical Aggression subscale (self-report)
description: Mean item score where higher indicates more aggression
notes: Published BPAQ-SF items: 'Given enough provocation, I may hit another person'; 'There are people who pushed me so far that we came to blows'; 'I have threatened people I know'. Mean of all three (1-5, 5 = very like me), else NA. When mapped, repeat its expression on beh_aggphys_self. Other forms, item subsets and other response scales go to beh_aggphys_self, and this row is then incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Verbal Aggression - Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire Short Form Verbal Aggression subscale (self-report)
description: Mean item score where higher indicates more aggression
notes: Published BPAQ-SF items: 'I often find myself disagreeing with people'; 'I can't help getting into arguments when people disagree with me'; 'My friends say that I'm somewhat argumentative'. Mean of all three (1-5, 5 = very like me), else NA.

label: Behaviour: Anger - Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire Short Form Anger subscale (self-report)
description: Mean item score where higher indicates more aggression
notes: Published BPAQ-SF items: 'Sometimes I fly off the handle for no good reason'; 'I have trouble controlling my temper'; 'I sometimes feel like a powder keg ready to explode'. Mean of all three (1-5, 5 = very like me), else NA. When mapped, repeat its expression on beh_anger_self. Other forms, item subsets and other response scales go to beh_anger_self, and this row is then incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Hostility - Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire Short Form Hostility subscale (self-report)
description: Mean item score where higher indicates more aggression
notes: Published BPAQ-SF items: 'At times I feel I have gotten a raw deal out of life'; 'Other people always seem to get the breaks'; 'I wonder why sometimes I feel so bitter about things'. Mean of all three (1-5, 5 = very like me), else NA.

label: Behaviour: Aggression - aggression scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's self-reported aggression scale, where higher indicates more aggression
notes: Multi-item aggression scale without BPAQ subscales; say in beh_agg_measure whether the sum or mean is mapped. A physical- or relational-only scale goes to beh_aggphys_self or beh_aggrel_self, and this row is then incompatible, naming it; a study total across forms stays here, and its physical and relational subscales also map there. Single items and item subsets of broader instruments are incompatible, named in source_columns, with a pointer to any row that holds them (BPAQ rows, beh_fight, beh_conduct_sdq_self). Parent- or carer-rated aggression and conduct scales go to beh_conduct_parent (SDQ and CBCL scores to their own rows), and teacher-rated aggression scales to beh_aggphys_teacher, beh_aggrel_teacher or beh_agg_teacher; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them.

label: Behaviour: Aggression measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_agg_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_agg_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Physical Aggression - physical aggression scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported physical aggression scale or subscale, where higher indicates more physical aggression
notes: Generic row for multi-item physical aggression scales or subscales (hitting, kicking, pushing, beating up, throwing things at or threatening others). When beh_aggphys_bpaq_self is mapped, repeat its expression here; other BPAQ physical forms and response scales come here instead. A study's aggression total stays on beh_agg_self and its physical subscale also maps here. An overt scale or subscale that adds verbal acts (insults, yelling) is partial where it is the study's physical form (e.g. released beside a relational subscale); a general aggression scale that mixes physical with verbal, relational or anger items and has no form subscales stays on beh_agg_self, and this row is then incompatible, naming it. Where a form is split by function (reactive, proactive), use the form total. Victimisation scales do not map here, and bullying-framed perpetration scales or subscales (e.g. a physical bullying subscale) are incompatible, named; they go to beh_bullied only. Single items, ad hoc item subsets and online-only scales are incompatible, pointing to any row that holds them (beh_fight). Teacher-rated physical aggression scales go to beh_aggphys_teacher; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Record the instrument and scoring in beh_aggphys_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Physical aggression measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_aggphys_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_aggphys_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format, item set or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Relational Aggression - relational aggression scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported relational aggression scale or subscale, where higher indicates more relational aggression
notes: Generic row for multi-item relational, indirect or social aggression scales or subscales (excluding others, spreading rumours, talking behind someone's back, turning others against someone, threatening to withdraw friendship). A study's aggression total stays on beh_agg_self and its relational subscale also maps here. Scales that add direct verbal acts (insults, name-calling) are partial; a general aggression scale that mixes relational with physical items and has no form subscales stays on beh_agg_self, and this row is then incompatible, naming it. Where a form is split by function (reactive, proactive), use the form total. Victimisation scales do not map here, and bullying-framed perpetration scales or subscales (e.g. a relational bullying subscale) are incompatible, named; they go to beh_bullied only. Single items, ad hoc item subsets and online-only scales are incompatible. Teacher-rated relational aggression scales go to beh_aggrel_teacher; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Record the instrument and scoring in beh_aggrel_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Relational aggression measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_aggrel_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_aggrel_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format, item set or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Anger - anger or anger-control-problems scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported anger or anger-control-problems scale (getting angry easily or intensely, temper outbursts, losing control when angry), where higher indicates more anger
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and published subscales of anger or anger-control problems: getting angry easily or intensely, temper outbursts, losing control when angry, outbursts at objects (e.g. the anger-control-problems scale of a broad self-report battery, a trait anger scale), in any rating format, compatible. When beh_agganger_bpaq_self is mapped, repeat its expression here; other forms of the BPAQ anger items (the full form's seven items, adapted wording, other response scales) come here instead. Anger outbursts at objects (throwing, breaking or slamming things when angry) are anger-control content; urges or acts to harm people (to beat, injure, hit or fight someone) are not, so a hostility scale that mixes anger with them (e.g. the SCL-90-R hostility subscale), and an anger scale that adds them, are partial; a scale presented as aggression that adds anger items stays on the aggression rows. Cognitive hostility (bitterness, resentment, suspicion; e.g. the BPAQ hostility items, beh_agghostility_bpaq_self), self-control and anger-management competence scales (beh_selfreg_self), emotion dysregulation scales (beh_emotdysreg_self) and aggression scales (beh_agg_self, beh_aggphys_self, beh_aggrel_self) are incompatible here, named. Single items (e.g. mh_irritable_self) and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Parent- and teacher-rated anger scales fill no row and are incompatible, named. Keyed higher = more anger; record the instrument and scoring in beh_anger_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Anger measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_anger_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_anger_self is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format, wording or item set from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Aggressive Cognitions - normative beliefs about aggression scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale of beliefs about how acceptable aggression is, where higher indicates more approval of aggression
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of normative beliefs about aggression, the participant's judgement of how acceptable or wrong it is to hit, push, shout at or say mean things to others, in general or in retaliation (e.g. the Normative Beliefs About Aggression Scale or an adapted version), in any rating format, compatible. Map the total approval score (general and retaliation items together) where released or scorable; a general-approval or retaliation-only subscale is partial where no total is in hand, and beh_aggcog_measure names it. A study's own set of items on how acceptable fighting is, with no published scale, is partial: score the share of approving answers over its approval items (e.g. disagreeing that fighting is wrong, agreeing that fighting is sometimes the only way to settle an argument), complete-case, with 'don't know' as NA, and name excitement, enjoyment and descriptive-norm items (e.g. everyone gets into fights) as unused. Keyed higher = more approval of aggression (reverse items rated from perfectly OK to really wrong). Attitudes to media or game violence, moral-disengagement scales, online-only items (e.g. whether it is acceptable to fight by text or online) and single items are incompatible, named. Cognitive hostility scales (e.g. the BPAQ hostility items, beh_agghostility_bpaq_self) and aggressive-behaviour scales stay on the aggression rows, and anger scales and hostility scales that mix anger with urges or acts to harm people (e.g. the SCL-90-R hostility subscale) go to beh_anger_self; none of them maps here. Record the instrument and scoring in beh_aggcog_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Aggressive Cognitions - hostile attribution bias (self-report)
description: Score on the study's vignette measure of hostile intent attribution, from the participant's judgements of whether peers in ambiguous provocations acted on purpose or to be mean, where higher indicates more hostile attributions
notes: Generic row for hostile attribution bias measured with ambiguous-provocation vignettes in which the participant judges whether a peer acted on purpose or to be mean (e.g. Crick's intent-attribution stories of physical and relational provocation), scored as the proportion, mean or count of hostile answers over the vignettes' intent questions, compatible. Map the total over all vignettes; a physical-only or relational-only vignette score is partial where no total is in hand. Emotional-reactivity or distress ratings and chosen responses asked with the vignettes are not attributions and are named as unused. Questionnaire hostility or suspicion scales (e.g. BPAQ Hostility) stay on their own rows and are incompatible here, named; single vignettes are incompatible. Keyed higher = more hostile attributions. Record the instrument, vignette and question counts and the scoring in beh_aggcog_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the vignettes or questions change.

label: Behaviour: Aggressive Cognitions - aggressive fantasy scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported scale of how often the participant imagines or daydreams about hurting others or other aggressive acts, where higher indicates more frequent aggressive fantasies
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of how often the participant imagines or daydreams about aggression: hitting or hurting someone, destroying enemies, people getting killed (e.g. the Aggressive Fantasy Scale), in any frequency format, compatible. A published fantasy scale is compatible as published, including any items it has on non-aggressive fantasies; a study's own item set that adds non-aggressive fantasy items is partial, and beh_aggcog_measure names them. Keyed higher = more frequent aggressive fantasies. Cognitive hostility scales (e.g. beh_agghostility_bpaq_self) and aggressive-behaviour scales stay on the aggression rows, and anger scales and hostility scales that mix anger with urges or acts to harm people go to beh_anger_self; all are incompatible here, named; single items are incompatible. Record the instrument and scoring in beh_aggcog_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Aggressive cognitions measure
description: Source instruments, item counts and item scoring behind the aggressive-cognition rows (beh_aggbeliefs_self, beh_agghostattrib_self and beh_aggfantasy_self)
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any aggressive-cognition row is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: 'normative beliefs: <instrument and score>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; hostile attribution: <instrument>, <v> vignettes, <q> of <Q> intent questions, <proportion|mean|count> of hostile answers (range <min>-<max>); aggressive fantasies: <instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', naming only the rows mapped, then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the missing-item rule and any change of response format, item set or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred; unavailable ('See beh_aggbeliefs_self.') only when every aggressive-cognition row is unavailable or incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Aggression - single item (teacher report)
description: Teacher's single-item rating of the child's aggressive behaviour towards others, where higher indicates more aggression
notes: One global teacher rating of the child's aggression towards others (e.g. how often the student behaves aggressively), rated by frequency or degree; an item on one form or act (hits others, excludes others) is partial. Reverse scales where the lowest number is most aggressive; record the scale points, anchors and recall period; standardise within dataset. Where two teachers rated the same item, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Disruption or misbehaviour in class goes to beh_disrupt_singleitem_teacher. Items and scores of truth-rated checklists (SDQ, TRF) and of other multi-item teacher scales are incompatible here: multi-item teacher aggression scales go to beh_aggphys_teacher, beh_aggrel_teacher or beh_agg_teacher, and the SDQ teacher conduct subscale stays on beh_conduct_sdq_teacher. A self- or parent-rated global item is incompatible, item named.

label: Behaviour: Disruptive behaviour - single item (teacher report)
description: Teacher's single-item rating of how often the child is disruptive or misbehaves in class, where higher indicates more disruptive behaviour
notes: One global teacher rating of how often the child is disruptive, misbehaves or causes trouble in class (e.g. how often the student is disruptive in your class), rated by frequency or degree; an item on one act (interrupts others' work, talks out of turn) is partial. Aggression towards others goes to beh_agg_singleitem_teacher. Reverse scales where the lowest number is most disruptive; record the scale points, anchors and recall period (a rating of the child in the teacher's current class needs no other window); standardise within dataset. Where two teachers rated the same item, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Items and scores of truth-rated checklists (SDQ conduct, TRF) and of other multi-item teacher scales are incompatible here: multi-item teacher aggression and attention scales go to the teacher aggression rows (beh_aggphys_teacher, beh_aggrel_teacher, beh_agg_teacher) or the teacher attention rows (beh_atten_teacher, beh_hyper_teacher, beh_adhdsymp_teacher), other multi-item teacher scales go to the generic teacher scale row of their construct where one exists (e.g. beh_socialskills_teacher) and otherwise fill no teacher row, and the SDQ teacher conduct subscale stays on beh_conduct_sdq_teacher. Yes/no school records (removed from class) and a self- or parent-rated item, including a report of teachers' complaints, are incompatible, item named; suspension and expulsion records go to beh_suspended.

label: Behaviour: Physical Aggression - physical aggression scale (teacher report)
description: Score on a teacher-rated scale or subscale of the child's physical (overt) aggression towards peers, where higher indicates more physical aggression
notes: Generic row for multi-item teacher-rated scales and subscales of physical or overt aggression towards peers: hitting, kicking, pushing, starting fights, threatening to hit or hurt (e.g. the overt aggression subscale of the Children's Social Behavior Scale teacher form or an adaptation, the physical items of a teacher-rated forms-and-functions aggression measure), in any rating format, a study's own scored scale included, compatible. A teacher aggression total across forms stays on beh_agg_teacher and its physical subscale also maps here. Where a form is split by function (reactive, proactive), use the form total. This row takes only scales whose items are all physical: a scale or subscale that mixes physical with verbal, relational, oppositional or anger items (e.g. an overt subscale that adds insults or yelling, a Teacher Report Form aggressive behaviour scale), and a narrow externalising scale of aggressive, oppositional and anger items (e.g. a Social Skills Rating System externalising subscale), go to beh_agg_teacher, and this row is then incompatible, naming them; a scale that adds hyperactivity-impulsivity items fills no teacher aggression row and is incompatible, named. Bullying-framed perpetration scales are incompatible, named, and victimisation scales do not map here. The SDQ teacher conduct subscale stays on beh_conduct_sdq_teacher and is incompatible here, named. Single teacher items go to beh_agg_singleitem_teacher, self-rated scales to beh_aggphys_self and parent-rated ones to beh_conduct_parent; all are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, applied to the teacher's ratings and keyed higher = more physical aggression. Where two teachers rated the child, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Record the instrument and rater in beh_teacher_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Relational Aggression - relational aggression scale (teacher report)
description: Score on a teacher-rated scale or subscale of the child's relational aggression towards peers, where higher indicates more relational aggression
notes: Generic row for multi-item teacher-rated scales and subscales of relational, indirect or social aggression: excluding a peer from the group, spreading rumours, ignoring a peer or threatening to end a friendship to hurt or control them, turning others against a peer (e.g. the relational aggression subscale of the Children's Social Behavior Scale teacher form or an adaptation, the relational items of a teacher-rated forms-and-functions aggression measure), in any rating format, a study's own scored scale included, compatible. A teacher aggression total across forms stays on beh_agg_teacher and its relational subscale also maps here. Where a form is split by function (reactive, proactive), use the form total. This row takes only scales whose items are all relational: a scale or subscale that mixes relational with direct verbal acts (insults, name-calling) or physical items, and a general aggression or narrow externalising scale, go to beh_agg_teacher, and this row is then incompatible, naming them; a scale that adds hyperactivity-impulsivity items fills no teacher aggression row and is incompatible, named. Score by the CBCL rule in the harmonisation guide; a released raw sum is divided by the number of items administered, with its missing-item rule recorded in beh_cbcl_measure ('rule not documented' if unknown); record the form and items administered in beh_cbcl_measure. A CBCL syndrome score: it stays on this row and never fills beh_peerprob_sdq_parent, beh_peerprob_makefriends or a generic parent row; it is neither internalising nor externalising and feeds no CBCL composite row. Parent report only: the Teacher's Report Form and Youth Self-Report scales of the same name never map here. Standardise within dataset, and within form where the form changes.

label: Behaviour: Externalising Problems - Child Behavior Checklist externalising score (parent/carer report)
description: Mean item score (0-2) across the form's Externalizing items (Aggressive + Rule-Breaking; Aggressive + Attention Problems on CBCL/1.5-5), where higher indicates more externalising problems
notes: Mean of answered items over the union of both component scales (an item on both counts once); NA unless each component was administered and has at least 80% of its administered items answered. Record the form and item counts in beh_cbcl_measure. Never pool with beh_ext_sdq_parent.

label: Behaviour: Child Behavior Checklist measure
description: Source CBCL form, item counts and item scoring behind the CBCL parent-report scores
missing_rule: Should not be missing when any beh_*_cbcl_parent or mh_*_cbcl_parent variable is available - using 'Unknown' as required
notes: Name the form, the items administered of the published total for each mapped scale, the item scoring and the missing-item rule; give one value per wave where forms differ. E.g. 'CBCL/6-18; aggressive 11 of 18, rule-breaking 9 of 17; 1-3 recoded to 0-2; mean of answered items, NA below 80%'. CBCL DSM-oriented scales and Total Problems map to the generic parent rows and are recorded in beh_parent_measure, not here.

label: Behaviour: Externalising - externalising problems scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's self-reported externalising-problems scale or screener, where higher indicates more externalising problems
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report screeners and scales that mix conduct, aggression, hyperactivity and inattention items (e.g. the GAIN-SS Externalizing Disorder Screener, scored as the past-year symptom count). Conduct-disorder or delinquency scales, and scales mixing conduct with oppositional items, go to beh_conduct_self and oppositional-defiant scales to beh_opp_self; they are incompatible here, named. SDQ and CBCL externalising composites stay on their own rows, parent- or carer-rated externalising scales go to beh_ext_parent, and impulsivity scales go to beh_impulsivity_self even when they include rule-breaking or aggressive items. Single items and item subsets of broader instruments are incompatible, and a score here does not also map to beh_agg_self, beh_aggphys_self, beh_aggrel_self or beh_atten_self. Record the instrument and scoring in beh_ext_measure; standardise within dataset.

label: Behaviour: Oppositional Behaviour - oppositional-defiant problems scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported oppositional-defiant behaviour scale or subscale, where higher indicates more oppositional behaviour
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and subscales of oppositional-defiant behaviour: defying or arguing with adults, refusing requests, deliberately annoying others, spite (e.g. the Youth Self-Report DSM-oriented Oppositional Defiant Problems scale, the defiant-behaviour scale of a broad self-report battery), in any rating format, compatible; a subscale that adds an off-construct item is partial. Conduct-disorder scales go to beh_conduct_self, and a study with both fills both; a scale that mixes oppositional with conduct items goes to beh_conduct_self (partial), and with no oppositional-only scale in hand this row is then incompatible, naming it. Anger and anger-control-problem scales go to beh_anger_self, SDQ conduct problems stays on beh_conduct_sdq_self and broadband screeners stay on beh_ext_self; all are incompatible here, named. Single items (e.g. beh_argues) and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Parent- or carer-rated oppositional scales go to beh_opp_parent and teacher ratings never fill this row; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Keyed higher = more oppositional behaviour; record the instrument and scoring in beh_ext_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Conduct Problems - conduct problems scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported conduct problems or delinquency scale (conduct-disorder behaviours such as aggression to people, destroying property, lying, theft and serious rule-breaking), where higher indicates more conduct problems
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales and subscales of conduct-disorder behaviour or delinquency: aggression to people or animals, destroying property, lying, theft, serious rule-breaking (e.g. the Youth Self-Report DSM-oriented Conduct Problems scale, a published self-reported delinquency scale), in any rating format, compatible. A scale that mixes oppositional with conduct items, and a study's documented count of delinquent acts that adds substance-use items, are partial; a study checklist with no documented score is incompatible, named. Oppositional-defiant scales go to beh_opp_self, and a study with both fills both. For the Youth Self-Report, map the DSM-oriented Conduct Problems scale where it can be scored and name the Rule-Breaking Behavior syndrome as unused. SDQ conduct problems stays on beh_conduct_sdq_self, broadband screeners mixing conduct with hyperactivity or inattention on beh_ext_self, and aggression scales on the aggression rows (beh_agg_self, beh_aggphys_self, beh_aggrel_self); all are incompatible here, named. Single items go to the act rows (beh_fight, beh_stealing, beh_vandalism, beh_truancy, beh_suspended) and are incompatible here, named. Parent- or carer-rated conduct scales go to beh_conduct_parent and teacher ratings never fill this row; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Keyed higher = more conduct problems; record the instrument and scoring in beh_ext_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Externalising, conduct and oppositional measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_ext_self, beh_conduct_self and beh_opp_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_ext_self, beh_conduct_self or beh_opp_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean|count>' for the one score row mapped; where two or three of beh_ext_self, beh_conduct_self and beh_opp_self are mapped, one such segment per row, prefixed 'externalising: ', 'conduct: ' and 'oppositional: ', naming each instrument; then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the off-construct items of a partial row, and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred; unavailable ('See beh_ext_self.') only when all three score rows are unavailable or incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Attention - inattention scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated inattention scale or subscale, where higher indicates more inattention
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of inattention alone (e.g. the inattention subscales of the Conners rating scales, SNAP-IV, ADHD Rating Scale, Vanderbilt or SWAN, and BASC-2 Attention Problems), compatible; a subscale that adds off-construct items (e.g. academic-skill items) is partial, and beh_parent_measure names them. When beh_atten_basc2 is mapped, repeat its expression here. A scale that mixes inattention with hyperactivity or impulsivity items, and a combined ADHD total or index, go to beh_adhdsymp_parent; with no inattention-only scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. SDQ hyperactivity/inattention and the CBCL Attention Problems syndrome stay on their own rows and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide and record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Hyperactivity-Impulsivity - hyperactivity-impulsivity scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated hyperactivity or hyperactivity-impulsivity scale or subscale, where higher indicates more hyperactivity and impulsivity
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of hyperactivity or hyperactivity-impulsivity without inattention items (e.g. the hyperactivity subscales of the Conners rating scales, SNAP-IV, ADHD Rating Scale, Vanderbilt or SWAN, and BASC-2 Hyperactivity), compatible; an impulsivity-only scale is partial. When beh_hyper_basc2 is mapped, repeat its expression here. A scale that mixes hyperactivity-impulsivity with inattention items, and a combined ADHD total or index, go to beh_adhdsymp_parent; with no hyperactivity-impulsivity scale free of inattention items in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. SDQ hyperactivity/inattention stays on beh_hyper_sdq_parent and is incompatible here, named; temperament activity-level, surgency and impulsivity scales go to beh_temp_surgency_parent and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide and record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: ADHD Symptoms - combined ADHD symptom scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale that combines inattention with hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms, or a released combined ADHD total or index, where higher indicates more ADHD symptoms
notes: Generic row for parent- or carer-rated scales that mix inattention with hyperactivity-impulsivity items and release no separate inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores (e.g. CBCL DSM-oriented Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Problems, Pediatric Symptom Checklist-17 attention, Brief Problem Monitor attention problems), and for a released combined ADHD total or index that is not the sum of scores mapped on beh_atten_parent and beh_hyper_parent (e.g. the Conners ADHD Index), compatible. A scale that adds off-construct items is partial (e.g. Behavior Problems Index hyperactive, with an obsessions item, or the Conners 10-item hyperactivity index, with three emotional-lability items). A released combined total that is the sum of an instrument's inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity subscales maps here only when those subscales are not released; where they are mapped and no other qualifying scale is in hand, this row is unavailable ('Derive at analysis from beh_atten_parent, beh_hyper_parent.'). SDQ hyperactivity/inattention and the CBCL Attention Problems syndrome stay on their own rows and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide and record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Oppositional Behaviour - oppositional-defiant problems scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated oppositional-defiant behaviour scale or subscale, where higher indicates more oppositional behaviour
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of oppositional-defiant behaviour (defiance, arguing, disobedience, temper, irritability, spite; e.g. the oppositional subscales of the Conners rating scales and SNAP-IV, CBCL DSM-oriented Oppositional Defiant Problems, an Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory oppositional scale), compatible; a subscale that adds an off-construct item (e.g. Behavior Problems Index headstrong, with a nervousness item) is partial. Conduct-disorder scales go to beh_conduct_parent, and a study with both fills both; a scale that mixes oppositional with conduct items, or an aggression-only scale, goes to beh_conduct_parent (partial), and with no oppositional-only scale in hand this row is then incompatible, naming it. Anger or irritability mood scales are incompatible, named. Broadband externalising scores go to beh_ext_parent. SDQ conduct problems and the CBCL Aggressive Behavior syndrome stay on their own rows and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide and record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Conduct Problems - conduct problems scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated conduct problems scale or subscale (conduct-disorder behaviours), where higher indicates more conduct problems
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of conduct-disorder behaviour (aggression to people or animals, destroying property, lying, theft, serious rule-breaking; e.g. CBCL DSM-oriented Conduct Problems, Behavior Problems Index antisocial), compatible. A scale that mixes oppositional with conduct items, or an aggression-only scale, is partial. Oppositional-defiant scales go to beh_opp_parent, and a study with both fills both. Broadband externalising scores go to beh_ext_parent. SDQ conduct problems and the CBCL Rule-Breaking and Aggressive Behavior syndromes stay on their own rows and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide and record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Externalising - externalising problems scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated broadband externalising-problems scale or composite, where higher indicates more externalising problems
notes: Generic row for the published externalising scale or composite of a parent- or carer-rated broadband instrument, combining oppositional, conduct or aggressive behaviour with or without attention-hyperactivity items (e.g. Behavior Problems Index externalising, Brief Problem Monitor or Brief Problem Checklist externalising, Pediatric Symptom Checklist-17 externalising, BITSEA externalising), compatible. A released externalising score maps here even when some of its items also feed scores on other parent rows; a released or computed composite that is exactly the plain sum of scores mapped on other generic parent rows is unavailable ('Derive at analysis from <rows>.'). The total of an ADHD and oppositional rating scale (e.g. SNAP-IV all items, a Conners short-form total) is incompatible, named. SDQ and CBCL externalising composites stay on beh_ext_sdq_parent and beh_ext_cbcl_parent and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide and record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Parent-rated scale measure
description: Source instrument, informant, item counts and item scoring behind the generic parent-report scale rows (beh_atten_parent, beh_hyper_parent, beh_adhdsymp_parent, beh_opp_parent, beh_conduct_parent, beh_ext_parent, mh_int_parent, mh_anx_parent, mh_dep_parent, mh_totalprob_parent, beh_selfreg_parent, beh_emotdysreg_parent, beh_emotreg_parent, beh_prosocial_parent and beh_socialskills_parent)
missing_rule: Should not be missing where any generic parent-report score row is non-missing; NA in waves where none was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument> (<informant>); attention: <scale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; hyperactivity: ...; combined ADHD: ...; oppositional: ...; conduct: ...; externalising: ...; internalising: ...; anxiety: ...; depression: ...; total: ...; self-regulation: ...; emotion dysregulation: ...; emotion regulation: ...; prosocial: ...; social skills: ...', naming only the rows mapped and each instrument where rows draw on different ones, then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed'), the facets averaged where no total is released, the missing-item rule, any averaging over two parents' ratings, the item counts by age where the item set changes with the child's age, and any change of response format, item set or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the instruments or forms change, and the forms by age group where the instrument changes with age. Status inferred; unavailable ('See beh_atten_parent.') only when every generic parent score row is unavailable or incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Prosocial Behaviour - online prosocial behaviour (self-report)
description: Total score for prosocial acts the participant performed towards others online or through electronic media, where higher indicates more frequent online prosocial behaviour
notes: Multi-item scale of prosocial acts the participant performed online (e.g. Online Prosocial Behaviour Scale); acts received from others do not map. Offline and general prosocial scales go to beh_prosocial_self. Never pool with beh_prosocial_sdq_* or beh_prosocial_self. Record the measure in beh_prosocial_online_measure.

label: Behaviour: Online prosocial behaviour measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_prosocial_online_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_prosocial_online_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>, <recall period>'. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Prosocial Behaviour - prosocial behaviour scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported prosocial behaviour scale, where higher indicates more prosocial behaviour
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of helping, sharing, comforting, cooperating or volunteering for others, offline or unspecified (e.g. the Prosocial Tendencies Measure, the Prosocialness Scale or a study item set), in any rating format. When beh_prosocial_sdq_self is mapped, repeat its expression here. Online-only scales go to beh_prosocial_online_self and are not repeated here. Scales of intentions or hypothetical vignettes, or limited to one kind of act or setting, are partial. Where a study's behaviour scale misses waves, an intention or hypothetical-helping vignette scale given in those waves fills them, and the row is then partial for that study (waves in notes). Where items have a not-applicable answer ('situation did not arise'), set it to NA and score the mean of the remaining items where at least half the scale's items have a substantive answer; record this in beh_prosocial_measure. Single items, acts received from others and moral-reasoning scales are incompatible; empathy scales go to beh_empathy_self and are incompatible here, named. Parent- or carer-rated prosocial scales go to beh_prosocial_parent, and teacher-rated ones to beh_prosocial_teacher. Record the instrument and scoring in beh_prosocial_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Prosocial behaviour measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_prosocial_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_prosocial_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items, how not-applicable answers were scored, and any change of response format, item set or recall period from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Prosocial Behaviour - prosocial behaviour scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale of the child's prosocial behaviour, where higher indicates more prosocial behaviour
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales and subscales of the child's helping, sharing, comforting or cooperating with others, in any rating format (e.g. the Child Prosociality Scale, the prosocial subscale of a parent form of the Preschool Social Behavior Scale), compatible. When beh_prosocial_sdq_parent is mapped, repeat its expression here, also where an adapted SDQ form is partial there. A scale limited to one kind of prosocial act (e.g. sharing only) or to one setting is partial. Broad social-skills or social-competence totals and their facet subscales go to beh_socialskills_parent; they and cooperation, manners or compliance scales with no helping, sharing or comforting item (e.g. co-operates with requests, waits turn, says please and thank you) are incompatible here, named. Where items have a not-applicable answer ('situation did not arise'), set it to NA and score the mean of the remaining items where at least half the scale's items have a substantive answer. Acts received from others, empathy or moral-reasoning scales, single items, study checklists with no published scoring and teacher ratings are incompatible, named; teacher-rated prosocial scales go to beh_prosocial_teacher. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more prosocial behaviour; record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Social Skills - social skills scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported social skills scale (cooperating, asserting oneself and getting along with others), where higher indicates more social skills
notes: Generic row for the total score of a multi-item self-report social skills scale (e.g. the Social Skills Rating System or Social Skills Improvement System student form total, a study's documented social skills scale), in any rating format, compatible. Where only facet subscales are released (e.g. cooperation, assertion), map the mean of the released facets other than self-control (as item means; the instrument's own empathy facet included), partial. The student form's self-control subscale stays on beh_selfreg_self and is never added here; prosocial behaviour scales go to beh_prosocial_self, standalone empathy scales to beh_empathy_self, and social self-concept, perceived social acceptance and self-rated social-competence scales to wb_selfconcept_social_self; a study's social-initiative scale (starting interactions with adults or peers) and peer-interaction scales fill no part of this row; all are incompatible here, named. Single items and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Parent- and teacher-rated scales go to beh_socialskills_parent and beh_socialskills_teacher and never pool here; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Keyed higher = more social skills; record the instrument and scoring in beh_socialskills_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Social skills measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_socialskills_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_socialskills_self is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and scale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the facets averaged where no total is released, the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or item set from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Social Skills - social skills or social competence scale (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale of the child's social skills or social competence (cooperating, asserting, getting along and interacting appropriately with others), where higher indicates more social skills
notes: Generic row for the total score of a multi-item parent- or carer-rated social skills or social competence scale (e.g. the Social Skills Improvement System or Social Skills Rating System parent social skills total, a published preschool social competence scale), in any rating format, compatible. Where only facet subscales are released (e.g. cooperation, assertion, responsibility), map the mean of the released facets other than self-control (as item means), partial. A scale that mixes social skills with approaches to learning, mastery or compliance items (e.g. a combined social skills and approaches-to-learning scale, the BITSEA competence scale, a positive behaviour scale) is partial, as is the social competence scale of the CBCL competence scales; the CBCL activities and total competence scores are named as unused, and CBCL school competence is not used here (it can fill acc_academachment_parentrated, partial). A self-control subscale goes to beh_selfreg_parent and is never added here; prosocial scales go to beh_prosocial_parent; positive peer-interaction and peer-play scales, SDQ peer problems and the CBCL Social Problems syndrome (beh_socprob_cbcl_parent) fill no part of this row; all are incompatible here, named. Single items and study checklists with no published scoring are incompatible, named. Self-report scales go to beh_socialskills_self and teacher ratings to beh_socialskills_teacher, and never pool here. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more social skills (reverse a scale of social-skill deficits); record the instrument in beh_parent_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave or age group where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Prosocial Behaviour - single item (teacher report)
description: Teacher's single-item rating of the child's helping or prosocial behaviour towards others, where higher indicates more prosocial behaviour
notes: One global teacher rating of the child's helping or prosocial behaviour towards others (e.g. how often the student helps others), rated by frequency or degree; an item on one kind of act (shares, comforts) is partial. Reverse scales where the lowest number is most prosocial; record the scale points, anchors and recall period; standardise within dataset. Where two teachers rated the same item, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Items and scores of truth-rated checklists (e.g. SDQ) and of other multi-item teacher scales are incompatible here: multi-item teacher prosocial scales go to beh_prosocial_teacher, and the SDQ teacher prosocial subscale stays on beh_prosocial_sdq_teacher. A self- or parent-rated global item is incompatible, item named.

label: Behaviour: Empathy - empathy scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's self-reported empathy scale, where higher indicates more empathy
notes: Generic row for multi-item self-report scales of empathy: sharing or concern for others' feelings (affective empathy) and understanding of others' feelings and views (cognitive empathy), e.g. the Basic Empathy Scale, Bryant's Index of Empathy, the Children's Empathic Attitudes Questionnaire, or the empathy subscale of a broader inventory. An instrument's empathy total, or a scale that covers both facets, is compatible; a scale or subscale of one facet only (e.g. Interpersonal Reactivity Index empathic concern or perspective taking, a Basic Empathy Scale facet alone) is partial. Where an instrument releases facet scores and defines a total, map the total as the manual defines it; where it defines none (e.g. the Interpersonal Reactivity Index), map the affective facet (empathic concern) and name the others as unused. Where two empathy scales were given on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then a dedicated empathy instrument over an empathy subscale of a broader inventory, then the scale with the most non-missing values, naming the other as unused. Prosocial behaviour scales stay on beh_prosocial_self; personal distress, fantasy, awareness of one's own emotions, emotion-recognition and theory-of-mind tasks, guilt, moral-reasoning and callous-unemotional scales, and single items are incompatible, named. Parent- or teacher-rated empathy scales are incompatible, named (no row holds them). Record the instrument and scoring in beh_empathy_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Behaviour: Empathy measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind beh_empathy_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_empathy_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscale or facet>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format, wording or item set from the published form; one value per wave where the items change. Status inferred.

label: Behaviour: Problematic screen use (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's scale of problematic, compulsive or dependent use of smartphones, the internet, games or social media, where higher indicates more problematic use
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of smartphone, internet, gaming or social-media addiction or dependence. Record the instrument, target and scoring in beh_problematicuse_measure; standardise within dataset. Single items are incompatible; time spent belongs in the st_* rows. Parent- or carer-rated scales go to beh_problematicuse_parent and never pool here; with no self-report scale in hand, this row is then incompatible, naming them. Where the better item set misses waves, a weaker set fills them (partial, waves in notes).

label: Behaviour: Problematic screen use (parent/carer report)
description: Score on a parent- or carer-rated scale of the child's problematic, compulsive or dependent use of screen media, smartphones, the internet, games or social media, where higher indicates more problematic use
notes: Generic row for multi-item parent- or carer-rated scales of the child's screen-media, smartphone, internet, gaming or social-media addiction or dependence, in any rating format (e.g. the Problematic Media Use Measure or its short form, the parent version of the Gaming Disorder Identification Scale, a study's documented parent-rated media addiction scale), compatible. A parent-completed form of an instrument written for self-report (e.g. an internet addiction test the parent answers about the child) is partial, as an adapted informant form; where the documentation does not say whether the parent rated the child's use or their own, it is incompatible, named. A follow-up item on how often the problems occurred (e.g. the past-year frequency item of the parent Gaming Disorder Identification Scale) is never added to the score and is named as unused. A parent's statements on what the child's media use costs (e.g. that the child would sleep more, behave better or do better at school with less media) are proximate: score the problem statements only and name any benefit statements as unused. A parent's own problematic use never fills this row. Single items, study checklists with no published scoring, cut-off classifications and time spent (st_* rows) are incompatible, named. Self-report scales go to beh_problematicuse_self and never pool here; teacher ratings fill no row and are incompatible, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more problematic use; record the instrument, target, informant and scoring in beh_problematicuse_measure. Where the better scale misses waves, a weaker one fills them (partial, waves in notes); standardise within dataset, and within wave where the scale or form changes.

label: Behaviour: Problematic screen use measure
description: Source measure, target, informant, item count and item scoring behind beh_problematicuse_self and beh_problematicuse_parent
missing_rule: Should not be missing where beh_problematicuse_self or beh_problematicuse_parent is non-missing; NA in waves where neither scale was administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified

When cog_execfunc_brief_parent or cog_execfunc_basc2 is mapped, repeat its expression here unchanged, a T-score included, with the named row's status; short, adapted and other forms of those instruments come here instead of the named row, compatible when cog_execfunc_measure describes them. Released subscales that together make up the instrument's total are summed to that total; otherwise subscale and index scores (e.g. inhibit, shift, working memory, planning, emotional control, the BRIEF indexes) never fill this row and are named as unused. An executive-function questionnaire other than the BRIEF and BASC-2 also gives its inhibitory-control subscale to beh_selfreg_parent, partial. Self-regulation and temperament scales (effortful control included, which stays on beh_selfreg_parent), attention-problem and ADHD scales (beh_atten_parent, beh_hyper_parent, beh_adhdsymp_parent), emotion regulation and dysregulation scales (beh_emotreg_parent, beh_emotdysreg_parent) and other problem scales never fill this row and are incompatible, named; child-performed tasks stay on the task rows (cog_atten_task, cog_flex_task, cog_inhib_task, cog_wm_task) and never pool here. Single items and study checklists with no published or documented scoring are incompatible, named; teacher ratings go to cog_execfunc_teacher and self-reports to cog_execfunc_self, and are incompatible here, named. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, keyed higher = more difficulties; where two questionnaires qualify on one occasion, map the named-row repeat first, then a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the others as unused. Released subscales that together make up the instrument's total are summed to that total; otherwise subscale and index scores never fill this row and are named as unused, and a teacher-rated inhibitory-control subscale fills no row. Self-regulation and temperament scales, attention-problem and ADHD scales (beh_atten_teacher, beh_hyper_teacher, beh_adhdsymp_teacher), emotion regulation and other problem scales never fill this row and are incompatible, named; child-performed tasks stay on the task rows (cog_atten_task, cog_flex_task, cog_inhib_task, cog_wm_task) and never pool here. Score by the parent-scale rule in the harmonisation guide, applied to the teacher's ratings; where two questionnaires qualify on one occasion, map a compatible scale over a partial one, then the one with the most non-missing values, and name the others as unused. Where two teachers rated the child, take one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and name the other as unused; never average them. Where the instrument or score form changes between waves (e.g. a T-score at one wave and a reversed raw mean at another), the row is partial, standardised within wave, and the change is named in cog_execfunc_measure. Record the instrument and rater in cog_execfunc_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave or form where the instrument or form changes.

An executive-function questionnaire other than the BRIEF and BASC-2 also gives its inhibitory-control subscale to beh_selfreg_self, partial. label: Mental Health: Unhealthy weight control - any unhealthy weight-control behaviour (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports any unhealthy weight-control behaviour (fasting, self-induced vomiting, laxatives or diet pills) during the study's recall period
notes: Self-reported behaviour to lose weight or avoid gaining it, under the binary behaviour rules: TRUE if any qualifying item is positive, FALSE if every answered qualifying item is no or never, NA if none is answered. Compatible behaviours: fasting or going without eating for a day (24 hours) or more, self-induced vomiting, laxatives and diet pills. Skipping meals and taking supplements, steroids or other medication (prescribed or not) for weight are partial: they qualify only where no compatible-behaviour item is in hand, and are otherwise named as unused. Healthy methods (exercise, eating less fat, sweets or soft drinks, eating more fruit, vegetables or protein, drinking water) never qualify, and neither do other methods not listed here (e.g. smoking to control weight, a one-food diet). Where the methods are asked only of participants who report trying to control their weight, those who report not trying are FALSE. Items asking only whether the participant is trying to lose weight, or is dieting, are incompatible, named. A parent-reported item is partial, under the binary behaviour rules; the participant's own report is used where it exists and the parent's is then named as unused. Record each wave's items and recall period: a window of two weeks to 12 months leaves the status unchanged, and a shorter window (e.g. the past seven days) or lifetime or unstated recall is partial. Not a diagnosis: eating-disorder diagnoses and eating-disorder symptom scale totals are incompatible, named; perceived body size goes to wb_bodyimage and body-satisfaction scales to wb_bodyesteem_self.

label: Wellbeing: Health-related Quality of Life - Child Health Utility 9D utility (self-report)
description: CHU-9D preference-weighted utility from the child's self-completed questionnaire, where higher indicates better health-related quality of life (1 = full health)
notes: Utility from the nine CHU-9D dimensions (worried, sad, pain, tired, annoyed, schoolwork or homework, sleep, daily routine, activities), each rated on five levels for today, completed by the child. Use the study's released utility as scored, naming its tariff in notes ('tariff not documented' if the documentation does not say), or score complete item sets with one published tariff (e.g. UK adult standard-gamble or Australian adolescent weights); NA where any dimension is unanswered, and one tariff per dataset. Adapted wording or response levels, including an added option the study scored, are partial; proxy-completed forms do not map. Some tariffs go below 0 (the Australian adolescent weights reach -0.1059), so no minimum is set. The dimension items are intensity ratings for today and never fill the frequency single-item rows or a generic scale row. Other preference-based utilities (e.g. EQ-5D-Y, HUI) and psychometric quality-of-life totals (PedsQL, KIDSCREEN) do not map here. Standardise within dataset.

Appearance satisfaction goes to wb_domainsat_appearance_self, life satisfaction to wb_lifesat_singleitem_self and happiness to wb_happiness_singleitem_self; single items on competence, one domain of self-concept or how far self-worth depends on others are incompatible, named. label: Wellbeing: Self-efficacy - academic self-efficacy scale (self-report)

notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of confidence in one's ability to learn, do school work and succeed at school across subjects (e.g. the Self-Efficacy Questionnaire for Children academic subscale, the PALS Academic Efficacy scale), including the efficacy subscale of a broader school-motivation or engagement scale and a published academic efficacy subscale whose items each name a subject (e.g. the Self-Efficacy for Academic Achievement subscale of Bandura's Children's Self-Efficacy Scale). A scale or subscale, published or documented, that mixes in self-concept items (comparisons with classmates, 'I am good at ...') is partial. Reverse negatively worded items so higher = more efficacious. Incompatible, named: single items and subject-specific efficacy scales (e.g. maths or English self-efficacy); a mean built from separate subject scales or subject items fills no row. General self-efficacy goes to wb_selfefficacy_self and academic self-concept to wb_selfconcept_academic_self. notes: '<instrument and subscale>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

A locus-of-control scale for one domain (e.g. academic or health locus of control) is partial. General self-efficacy scales go to wb_selfefficacy_self, academic self-efficacy scales to wb_selfefficacy_academic_self and self-esteem scales to wb_selfesteem_self; none of them fills this row. Single items are incompatible, named; a parent's own mastery or locus of control never maps here. Record the instrument and scoring in wb_control_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change.

label: Wellbeing: Self-concept - academic self-concept scale (self-report)

notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of general academic or school self-concept, covering school work as a whole (e.g. Self-Description Questionnaire I or II General School or III General Academic, Harter Scholastic Competence, Piers-Harris Intellectual and School Status, AF5 academic); Marsh's Self-Description Questionnaire is not the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. Reverse negatively worded items so higher = more positive. Maths, verbal and science self-concept scales and items go to wb_selfconcept_maths_self, wb_selfconcept_verbal_self and wb_selfconcept_science_self, and a composite across subjects, such as a Self-Description Questionnaire Total Academic score that adds the subject scales, maps to none of the self-concept rows (incompatible, named). Single items are incompatible, named; an overall rating of grades or standing goes to acc_academachment_selfrated. Academic self-efficacy scales go to wb_selfefficacy_academic_self. School belonging, satisfaction with school or school work and quality-of-life school scales do not map here; global self-worth goes to wb_selfesteem_self. Record the instrument and scoring of every self-concept row in wb_selfconcept_measure; standardise within dataset. NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Wellbeing: Self-concept - maths self-concept scale (self-report)
