notes: Generic row for multi-item maths self-concept scales, a study's own item set included (e.g. Self-Description Questionnaire Mathematics or Math, or a large-scale assessment's mathematics self-concept or confidence scale); scoring as wb_selfconcept_academic_self. A single item rating the participant's own competence in maths (e.g. 'I am good at maths'), or an item subset of a broader instrument not given for maths self-concept, is partial; name the items in notes. Incompatible, named: maths self-efficacy scales, maths anxiety, interest or value measures on their own, maths grades or marks, and ratings by others. A composite across subjects maps to none of the self-concept rows. Record the instrument and scoring in wb_selfconcept_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change. NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Wellbeing: Self-concept - verbal self-concept scale (self-report)

notes: Generic row for multi-item verbal self-concept scales on reading or the language of instruction, a study's own item set included (e.g. Self-Description Questionnaire Reading or Verbal, or a large-scale assessment's reading self-concept scale); where reading self-concept is released as separate competence and difficulty scales, map the competence scale; scoring as wb_selfconcept_academic_self. English counts only where it is the language of instruction. A single item rating the participant's own competence in reading or that language (e.g. 'I am good at English' in an English-language school), or an item subset of a broader instrument not given for verbal self-concept, is partial; name the items in notes. Incompatible, named: self-concept in a foreign or second language taught as a subject (English included where it is not the language of instruction), verbal self-efficacy scales, reading or language anxiety, interest or value measures on their own, grades or marks, and ratings by others. A composite across subjects maps to none of the self-concept rows. Record the instrument and scoring in wb_selfconcept_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change. label: Wellbeing: Self-concept - science self-concept scale (self-report)

notes: Generic row for multi-item science self-concept scales, a study's own item set included (e.g. a large-scale assessment's science self-concept or confidence scale); scoring as wb_selfconcept_academic_self. A scale on one science subject (e.g. physics) is partial, and so is a single item rating the participant's own competence in science or one science subject (e.g. 'I am good at science') or an item subset of a broader instrument not given for science self-concept; name the items in notes. Incompatible, named: science self-efficacy scales, science anxiety, interest or value measures on their own, grades or marks, and ratings by others. A composite across subjects maps to none of the self-concept rows. Record the instrument and scoring in wb_selfconcept_measure; standardise within dataset, and within wave where the items change. NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Wellbeing: Self-concept - social self-concept scale (self-report)
description: Score on the study's scale of social self-concept (the participant's view of their own acceptance by and ease with peers), where higher indicates a more positive social self-concept
notes: Generic row for multi-item scales of peer or social self-concept or perceived social acceptance (e.g. Self-Description Questionnaire I Peer Relations or II Same-Sex Relations, Harter Social Acceptance, Piers-Harris Popularity, AF5 social); scoring as wb_selfconcept_academic_self. A self-rated social-competence scale that mixes in support or companionship items is partial. Incompatible, named: single items (difficulty making friends goes to beh_peerprob_makefriends), teacher ratings and peer nominations of acceptance, and friendship or peer-relationship quality scales (companionship, disclosure, conflict). Romantic, opposite-sex and parent-relations self-concept, perceived support (wb_socsupport_friends_self), loneliness (mh_lonely_scale_self), social anxiety (mh_socanx_self), social skills scales (beh_socialskills_self) and quality-of-life peer subscales do not map here, and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire peer problems subscales (beh_peerprob_sdq_*) and school belonging or connectedness scales (acc_schoolbelonging_self) neither map nor repeat here. label: Wellbeing: Self-concept measure
description: Source measure, item counts and item scoring behind the self-concept rows (wb_selfconcept_academic_self, wb_selfconcept_maths_self, wb_selfconcept_verbal_self, wb_selfconcept_science_self and wb_selfconcept_social_self)

description: Participant's rating of their own mental or emotional health
notes: Self-report only; proxy ratings, ratings relative to peers and ratings of change over time are not mapped. Recode as wb_selfratedhealth_self: four-level excellent/good/fair/poor maps by label, leaving Very good unused; symmetric five-level scales map by rank and are proximate.

label: Wellbeing: Positive affect - total score (self-report, any instrument)
description: Total positive affect score as scored by the source study, where higher indicates more frequent positive feelings
notes: Published positive-affect scale or subscale (e.g. PISA 2018 positive affect, PANAS-C PA), even if it shares an item with another mapped scale, compatible. A study's own set of two or more positive-feeling items with no published scoring (e.g. the positive half of a survey's feelings battery, or a study composite of diary or experience-sampling positive emotion ratings such as happy, relaxed or content): sum or mean the positive-feeling items asked at every wave, complete-case, partial, or use the study's released composite of them; an experience-sampling or diary composite is the person mean over the burst. Energy or vitality items (e.g. energetic, full of energy) are not positive-feeling items: they never count toward the two, are left out of the sum, and a released composite that includes one is not used. Single mood items are not mapped (a lone happiness rating goes to wb_happiness_singleitem_self), nor are ad hoc sums of another instrument's items. Subscales and totals of depression, anxiety, stress and distress inventories (e.g. CES-D positive affect) stay with their inventory and are incompatible here, named. Incompatible, named: affect felt during one activity (e.g. while gaming), parent-rated or parent-proxy scales, and temperament positive affectivity or surgency scales. The instrument's negative-affect scale goes to wb_negaffect_self and a study's own negative-feeling items to mh_distress_self; totals or balance scores combining positive and negative affect are not mapped. Record the measure in wb_posaffect_measure; standardise within dataset.

label: Wellbeing: Positive affect measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_posaffect_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_posaffect_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

notes: Published negative-affect scale or subscale (e.g. PANAS or PANAS-C negative affect, SPANE negative feelings), even if it shares an item with another mapped scale. A study's own set of negative-feeling items with no published scoring (e.g. the negative half of a survey's feelings battery, or a study composite of diary or experience-sampling emotion ratings) is a study checklist on mh_distress_self and is incompatible here, named. Single mood items and ad hoc sums of another instrument's items are not mapped. Depression, anxiety, stress and distress inventories, their subscales (e.g. CES-D depressed affect) and totals stay on the mental-health rows and are incompatible here, named. Incompatible, named: affect felt during one activity (e.g. while gaming), parent-rated or parent-proxy scales and temperament negative affectivity, and totals or balance scores combining positive and negative affect. A score here does not also map to mh_distress_self, mh_dep_self or mh_anx_self. Record the measure in wb_negaffect_measure; standardise within dataset.

label: Wellbeing: Negative affect measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_negaffect_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_negaffect_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Eudaimonic wellbeing - total score (self-report, any instrument)
description: Total eudaimonic wellbeing score as scored by the source study, where higher indicates greater eudaimonic wellbeing
notes: Multi-item eudaimonic scale scored as a whole: purpose, meaning, self-realisation, effortful engagement (e.g. QEWB, Flourishing Scale, PISA meaning in life). Single items, grit, EPOCH subscales and parent-rated flourishing are not mapped. Do not pool with WEMWBS, SWEMWBS or WHO-5. Record the measure in wb_eudaimonic_measure.

label: Wellbeing: Eudaimonic wellbeing measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_eudaimonic_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_eudaimonic_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Perceived support from family (self-report)
description: Score on the study's scale of perceived social support from family, where higher indicates more support
notes: Generic row for family-support scales or subscales (e.g. the MSPSS family subscale). Only items on support the child receives or can call on (help, understanding, someone to talk to or confide in). Parenting behaviours, family involvement (talk, meals, interest in schoolwork), parenting-style and monitoring items are incompatible; child-reported parental monitoring or knowledge scales go to fam_monitoring_self, relationship or attachment scales to fam_parentchild_rel_self, and family functioning, cohesion or conflict scales to fam_functioning_self and fam_conflict_self. A published support subscale that mixes in companionship items is partial. Record the instrument and scoring of both support rows in wb_socsupport_measure; standardise within dataset.

label: Wellbeing: Perceived support from friends (self-report)
description: Score on the study's scale of perceived social support from friends, where higher indicates more support
notes: Generic row for friend-support scales or subscales (e.g. the MSPSS friends subscale); item scope as wb_socsupport_family_self. Companionship items (time or fun with friends) are not support; a subscale mixing them in is partial. Counts of friends are incompatible.

label: Wellbeing: Perceived social support measure
description: Source measure, item counts and item scoring behind wb_socsupport_family_self and wb_socsupport_friends_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where either support score is non-missing; NA in waves where the scales were not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>; family: <k> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; friends: ...'. Status inferred.

label: Health: Sleep duration on weekdays
description: Usual sleep duration on school nights or weekdays
notes: Hours asleep. Time of falling or going to sleep to waking is compatible (unless banded); bedtime or lights-out to waking is partial; never subtract a separate sleep-latency item. An open band takes the bound its label states, or half an hour beyond a neighbouring point label ('less than 6 hours' next to '6 hours' = 5.5); the share in an open band does not lower the status. Keep durations under 4 or over 16 hours; they are screened at analysis. Record the respondent.

label: Health: Sleep duration on weekends
description: Usual sleep duration on weekend or non-school nights
notes: As hlth_sleep_wd.

label: Health: Sleep duration on an average night
description: Usual sleep duration on an average night
notes: 5:2 weighted mean of hlth_sleep_wd and hlth_sleep_we where both exist; otherwise a usual-night item. As hlth_sleep_wd for clock times, bands and implausible values.

label: Health: Sleep problems score
description: Total score on the study's sleep-problems scale, where higher indicates more problems
notes: Generic row for multi-item sleep-problem scales (e.g. the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children). Record the instrument and respondent in hlth_sleepprob_measure; standardise within dataset. Single items are incompatible here, named: items on trouble falling or staying asleep, night waking or sleeping poorly go to hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_self or hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_parent, and the HBSC-SCL sleep item stays on wb_psychcomplaints_diffsleep.

label: Health: Sleep problems measure
description: Source measure, respondent, item count and item scoring behind hlth_sleepprob
missing_rule: Should not be missing where hlth_sleepprob is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument> (<self|parent> report), <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>'. Status inferred.

label: Health: Sleep problems - single item (self-report)
description: Self-reported frequency of trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, waking in the night or sleeping poorly, from a single item
notes: Self-report single items on how often the child has trouble falling asleep, has trouble staying asleep or wakes in the night, or sleeps poorly (e.g. 'How often do you have trouble going to sleep or staying asleep?'). Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide): anchors map by wording, night counts by their share of a known recall window, labels the source cannot reach are named, and a source with fewer than five levels is proximate; record the recall period, which does not change the status. An item pooling these complaints is compatible; where they are asked as separate items, take the most frequent level across the answered items and name each. An item also scored in a mapped scale (hlth_sleepprob, or a somatic, depression or distress scale) fills this row when it matches in wording; note 'also scored in <row>'. The HBSC-SCL 'difficulty getting to sleep' item, and the identical adaptation wb_psychcomplaints_diffsleep takes, stay on that row and are incompatible here, named. Incompatible, item named: yes/no items; truth, agreement, intensity and distress ratings; global sleep-quality ratings (e.g. the PSQI quality rating, how refreshing sleep is) and 'enough sleep' items (enough sleep, less sleep than you should); duration, bedtime, waking time and latency, including how often the child falls asleep within a stated time; daytime sleepiness or tiredness; nightmares; items pooling these complaints with any of those; and items attributing poor sleep to a cause such as screen use or worry. Only the child's own answers: proxy answers, and answers the study filled in from a donor for a proxy interview, are NA, counted in notes with the study's proxy or imputation flag named. A parent's report goes to hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_parent; a teacher's rating fills neither row. Never carried across waves.

label: Health: Sleep problems - single item (parent report)
description: Parent or carer's report of how often the child has trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, wakes in the night or sleeps poorly, from a single item
notes: Proxy counterpart of hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_self: the same scope, Frequency-item rules (applied to the parent's ratings), pooling rule, HBSC-SCL rule and incompatible items apply, with these differences. An item scored in a mapped scale (hlth_sleepprob or a parent problem checklist) is not repeated here; with only such items in hand this row is incompatible, naming them and the row that holds them. Bedtime resistance, sleeping alone or in the parents' bed, regular bedtimes and other sleep routines are incompatible, named, as are counts of wakings per night; counts of nights with waking in a known window map by the day-share cuts. A parent's or carer's rating of the child only; record the informant. The child's own report goes to hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_self, and a teacher's rating fills neither row. Never carried across waves.

label: Health: Body mass index
description: The child's body mass index at the occasion
notes: Weight in kg / height in metres squared, measured or reported (self or parent), as the study releases it or computed in the expression from height and weight (pounds and inches: x 703). Where the study also releases a version cleared of biologically implausible values, use the uncleaned or computed BMI and name the cleaned version as unused. Clear zero, negative and sentinel codes. A top- or bottom-coded height or weight takes its bound (name it); partial where more than about 5% of values sit at one code. Keep every other value as entered, including extreme values and entries only possible in another unit (e.g. a height of 1.26 in a cm field), never repaired; they are screened at analysis. Where one occasion has more than one source, take measured, then the child's own report, then a parent's report, and name the others as unused. BMI-for-age z-scores, percentiles and weight-status categories are derived at analysis from BMI, age and sex; a study that releases z-scores but neither BMI nor the height and weight to compute it maps them to hlth_bmi_z, and one that releases only percentiles or weight-status categories is incompatible, item named. Record the source in hlth_bmi_measure. Height and weight of the occasion only: never carried across waves. A parent's own BMI is incompatible.

label: Health: BMI source
description: How the height and weight behind hlth_bmi or hlth_bmi_z were obtained
missing_rule: Should not be missing where hlth_bmi or hlth_bmi_z is non-missing; NA in waves where neither is mapped; 'Unknown' only when a value exists but its source cannot be identified
notes: Measured: height and weight measured by study staff or taken from health records. Self-reported: the child's own report. Parent-reported: a parent's or carer's report, including a parent copying a recent measurement. Constant per dataset and wave where one source applies; where the source differs between rows of a wave (e.g. teens report their own, younger children's parents report theirs), the value follows the row. Status inferred, or compatible where a source column records the source per row.

label: Health: BMI-for-age z-score (released)
description: The child's BMI-for-age z-score at the occasion as released by the study, against a named growth reference
notes: Only for a study that releases BMI-for-age z-scores but neither the child's BMI nor the height and weight to compute it: map the released z-score as scored, name its growth reference in hlth_bmi_z_measure and record the height and weight source in hlth_bmi_measure. Where hlth_bmi is mapped, this row is unavailable ('Derive at analysis from hlth_bmi.'), whether or not the study also releases a z-score, because z-scores are derived at analysis on one reference. BMI-for-age percentiles and weight-status categories are incompatible, item named, and are never converted to z-scores; weight-for-age, weight-for-length and height-for-age z-scores and a parent's own BMI are incompatible, item named. Keep every released value; extreme values are screened at analysis. Height and weight of the occasion only: never carried across waves.

label: Health: BMI z-score reference
description: Growth reference and scoring behind hlth_bmi_z
missing_rule: Should not be missing where hlth_bmi_z is non-missing; NA in waves where hlth_bmi_z is not mapped; 'Unknown' only when a z-score exists but its growth reference cannot be identified
notes: '<growth reference and version>, BMI-for-age z-score, <age range scored>', naming the reference as the study documents it (e.g. WHO 2007 growth reference, WHO 2006 child growth standards, CDC 2000 growth charts, IOTF). One value per dataset and wave. Status inferred.

label: Health: Pubertal status
description: The child's pubertal status at the occasion on a published measure (Pubertal Development Scale, Tanner stage), where higher indicates more advanced development
notes: Generic row for the child's pubertal status as the instrument scores it, higher = more advanced: the Pubertal Development Scale mean of its sex-specific items (1-4; menarche no = 1, yes = 4) or its released category score (1-5), and Tanner stage (1-5), self-rated from drawings or descriptions, parent-rated or examiner-assessed, the mean of the breast or genital and pubic-hair stages where both are rated. Compatible from any informant, item subsets and adapted forms included; record the measure, informant, items and scoring in hlth_puberty_measure. A released score averaged over answered items is used only where at least half were answered. Standardise within dataset, sex and measure at analysis, and within wave where the measure changes. Where one occasion has more than one source, take the examiner's assessment, then the child's own report, then a parent's report, and name the others as unused; where one source gives two measures on one occasion, take the measure the dataset uses at the most occasions (else the Pubertal Development Scale) and name the other as unused. Proximate, item named: an onset item alone (whether puberty, its body changes, menarche or first nocturnal emission have started: not started = 0, started = 1), and menarche alone, including an age at menarche read against the age at the occasion (at or below it = 1, otherwise 0). Incompatible, item named: perceived timing relative to peers ('earlier or later than others your age'), single body-change items outside a published measure, hormone levels and bone age. Anthropometric maturity offsets go to hlth_maturity_offset. Never carried across waves.

label: Health: Pubertal status measure
description: Source measure, informant, item count and scoring behind hlth_puberty_status
missing_rule: Should not be missing where hlth_puberty_status is non-missing; NA in waves where no pubertal measure was given; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its measure cannot be identified
notes: '<measure> (<examiner|self|parent>), <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <mean|stage|category score|onset indicator|menarche indicator>', then the items by sex, any adaptation, and the source order where an occasion had more than one source. One value per wave. Status inferred.

label: Health: Somatic maturity offset
description: Years from the child's predicted age at peak height velocity at the occasion (negative: before it), from an anthropometric equation
notes: The maturity offset of the Mirwald (2002) or Moore (2015) equations, as the study releases it or computed in the expression from the occasion's measured height, sitting height, weight and decimal age with the published sex-specific coefficients; name the equation and the measures used (compatible). An offset whose equation the study does not document is partial. Predicted age at peak height velocity is the age at measurement minus the offset and has no row; where a study releases it without the offset, the offset is the decimal age at measurement minus it. Other maturity estimates (percentage of predicted adult height, skeletal age) and pubertal status measures (hlth_puberty_status) are incompatible here, named. Keep every value, including values beyond the equation's validation range; they are screened at analysis. Never carried across waves.

label: Health: Days physically active for at least 60 minutes
description: Number of days in the past week or a usual week on which the child was physically active for a total of at least 60 minutes
notes: The common moderate-to-vigorous activity item: on how many days the child was physically active for a total of at least 60 minutes per day, over the past 7 days or in a usual week (both compatible; where a study asks both, take the past 7 days and name the other as unused; never average them). Self or parent report; record the informant and the recall. Day bands at their midpoint (1-3 = 2, 4-6 = 5, 5-6 = 5.5), 'every day' = 7, partial; write the band values in notes. Items with another minimum duration (20 or 30 minutes, 3 hours of active play), days of vigorous activity or of sport or exercise, hours or minutes of activity, device-measured activity, participation (yes/no) and guideline flags ('60 minutes on 5 or more days', 'meets the recommendation') are incompatible, item named. Never carried across waves.

label: Health: Birth weight
description: The child's weight at birth in grams
notes: The child's own weight at birth, from records or parent recall; record which and the informant. Grams as entered; kg x 1,000; pounds and ounces (lb x 16 + oz) x 28.35. A top or bottom code takes its bound (name it); partial where more than about 5% of values sit at one code. Bands: closed bands at their midpoint, an open band half the neighbouring band's width beyond its bound ('under 2,500 g' next to '2,500-2,999 g' = 2,250; '4,500 g or more' next to '4,000-4,499 g' = 4,750), partial; write the open-band values in notes. Low-birth-weight flags and size-for-gestational-age categories with no weight are incompatible, item named. Keep every value as entered, including values under 500 g or over 6,000 g and entries only possible in another unit (e.g. 26 or 99.6 in a kg field), never repaired; they are screened at analysis. A sibling's or a parent's own birth weight is incompatible. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule).

label: Health: Born preterm
description: Whether the child was born before 37 completed weeks of gestation
notes: TRUE before 37 completed weeks of gestation, FALSE at 37 weeks or later. Gestational age in completed weeks: under 37 = TRUE; where the study classifies its weeks as preterm or term, use that classification. 'Born more than 3 weeks before the due date' is compatible; '3 weeks or more before the due date' (the bound inclusive) is partial. A yes/no item with another cut (more than 2 or 4 weeks early, before 36 weeks) or with no stated cut ('born premature?'), and a cut the source's format forces (weeks heaped at month multiples), are partial; name the cut. Records or parent recall; record which and the informant. Neonatal care items (incubator, intensive care) are incompatible, item named. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule).

label: Health: Ever breastfed
description: Whether the child was ever breastfed or fed breast milk
notes: TRUE if the child ever received breast milk (breastfed or expressed milk), FALSE if never. A duration item is TRUE for any duration above zero (less than a month and still breastfeeding included) and FALSE for never or did not breastfeed. Free-text durations are parsed in the expression (partial); answers that cannot be read are NA, counted in notes. An item on a recent window only ('currently breastfed', 'in the past month') is incompatible unless the window spans the child's whole life at that interview. Exclusive-breastfeeding items are incompatible, item named. Record the informant. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule).

label: Health: Mother smoked in pregnancy
description: Whether the child's mother smoked tobacco during the pregnancy with the child
notes: TRUE if the mother smoked tobacco at any point in the pregnancy (any amount, any trimester), FALSE if she did not. The mother's own report or the other parent's; record the informant and when it was asked. Items on separate parts of the pregnancy combine (TRUE if any is TRUE); an item on one part only (a trimester, at booking) is partial. Smoking-status categories that cannot place quitting before or during the pregnancy are NA, partial. The mother's smoking at another time, the father's or household smoking and exposure to others' smoke are incompatible, item named. E-cigarettes alone are incompatible; items pooling them with tobacco are partial. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule).

label: Health: Chronic physical health condition - diagnosed
description: Whether a health professional has ever told the respondent the child has a long-standing physical health condition (e.g. asthma, diabetes, epilepsy or a heart condition), and whether the child currently has it
notes: Never = never told; Previously = told, not current; Currently = told and current. Any long-standing physical health condition a health professional diagnosed (e.g. asthma, diabetes, epilepsy, a heart condition, cancer, arthritis, cerebral palsy, a kidney or bowel disease); where conditions are asked as separate items, a child told of any counted condition is told, and currently has one if any told item is current. A checklist ending in an 'other long-standing condition' item is compatible on scope; a checklist without one, or an item on one condition only (e.g. asthma alone), is partial; name the conditions asked. Hay fever, food allergy and eczema do not count alone, nor does an allergy item that does not separate them: their items are named unused, and an any-condition flag or count that includes them is partial. Mental, behavioural, developmental and learning conditions do not count: ADHD, autism, conduct, anxiety, depression, learning disability and speech or language conditions have their own diagnosis rows, intellectual disability (mental retardation), emotional disturbance and developmental delay are named unused, and an any-condition flag that includes any of them is incompatible, named. A binary ever-told item: told = Currently, not told = Never (partial); it does not fill waves of a row whose other waves separate current from previous diagnosis, which stay NA. Where a wave skips children already reported told of a condition at an earlier interview, a skipped child whose latest earlier answer was told takes Currently (partial), and the notes name the routing. Treatment or medication for a told condition, or being told within a recent recall window, as proxy for current: partial. Not attributed to a health professional (a parent's or the child's report that the child has a condition, a long-standing illness item with no diagnosis): incompatible, item named. A stem that pools educators with health professionals ('a doctor, other health care provider, or educator ever told you') counts as attributed to a health professional, with no loss of status. Incompatible, item named: items pooling a diagnosis with referral or suspicion; treatment, medication or help-seeking with no told condition; acute illnesses, injuries and symptoms; and general-health ratings (wb_generalhealth_parent, wb_selfratedhealth_self). Disability, impairment and activity-limitation items go to hlth_disability. Not a severity rating. Record the informant and the conditions asked.

label: Health: Disability or activity-limiting condition
description: Whether the child has a long-term physical, sensory or other health condition or impairment that limits daily activities, or is identified as having a disability
notes: TRUE for an identified disability or a long-term limitation of daily activities by a health condition, FALSE for neither; record the informant and the definition. Compatible: an item on whether the child has, or identifies as having, a disability (e.g. 'Do you identify as a person with a disability?'), and a long-term limitation of the kind or amount of activity at home, school, work or play because of a physical condition or health problem (TRUE where limited, FALSE where there is no condition or it does not limit). Partial: such a long-term limitation item that pools physical with mental conditions (e.g. 'because of a physical or mental condition or health problem'), scored the same way, the pooling named; a registered or certified disability (an official registration, card or grade), TRUE for any registered physical, sensory or other health type; and a frequency item on how often a health problem limits or stops the child's activities, TRUE above never, FALSE for never. Proximate: such a frequency item that pools health with emotional problems, TRUE above never; name the pooling. Where impairments or conditions are asked as separate items (e.g. visual, hearing, orthopaedic, other health impairment), TRUE if any physical, sensory or other health item is positive, FALSE if every answered item is negative, NA if none is answered. Learning, intellectual, developmental, speech or language and emotional or behavioural items alone do not count: they are named unused and never make the row TRUE. A released composite or flag that pools them with other conditions is not used: score the separate physical, sensory and other health items where they are released, else the row is incompatible, naming it. Incompatible, item named: a long-standing illness or disability item with no limitation wording (e.g. 'any long-standing illness, disability or infirmity'); a told diagnosis with no disability or limitation wording (hlth_chroniccond_diagnosed or the condition's own diagnosis row); counts of days in bed, off school or with reduced activity in a recent window; special educational needs or IEP status; a parent's or sibling's disability; and general-health ratings. Where the child and a parent both report on one occasion, take the report of the row's screen-time respondent (st_responder) and name the other as unused. Never carried across waves.
